| Casualties |
| Deaths | **55 total:**<sup about="#mwt15" id="cite_ref-LASpreadsheet_2-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;LASpreadsheet&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-LASpreadsheet-2&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-LASpreadsheet-2" id="mwDg"><span id="mwDw"><span id="mwEA">[</span>2<span id="mwEQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

-   36 homicides, including 23 unsolved
-   11 killed by police and the National Guard
-   8 indirect deaths considered riot-related<sup about="#mwt18" id="cite_ref-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;group&quot;:&quot;lower-alpha&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-3&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-3" data-mw-group="lower-alpha" id="mwEg"><span id="mwEw"><span id="mwFA">[</span>a<span id="mwFQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

 |
| Injuries | 2,567 |
| Arrested | 12,200<sup about="#mwt22" id="cite_ref-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-4&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-4" id="mwFg"><span id="mwFw"><span id="mwGA">[</span>3<span id="mwGQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt27" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-5&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-5" id="mwGg"><span id="mwGw"><span id="mwHA">[</span>4<span id="mwHQ">]</span></span></a></sup> |
| Damage | $1 billion |

Los Angeles, California, experienced a series of riots and civil disturbances from April 29 to May 3, 1992.<sup about="#mwt32" id="cite_ref-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-6" id="mwHw"><span id="mwIA"><span id="mwIQ">[</span>5<span id="mwIg">]</span></span></a></sup> Civil unrest began in [South Central Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Los_Angeles "South Los Angeles") on April 29, after a jury [acquitted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acquittal "Acquittal") four officers of the [Los Angeles Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Police_Department "Los Angeles Police Department") (LAPD) charged with using [excessive force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_brutality "Police brutality") in the arrest and beating of [Rodney King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_King "Rodney King"). The incident had been videotaped by George Holiday, who was a bystander to the incident, and was heavily reported on by various news and media outlets.

The rioting took place in several areas in the [Los Angeles metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Los_Angeles "Greater Los Angeles") as thousands of people rioted over six days following the verdict's announcement. Widespread [looting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looting "Looting"), [assault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assault "Assault"), and [arson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arson "Arson") occurred during the riots, which local police forces had difficulty controlling. The situation in the Los Angeles area was resolved after the [California National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_National_Guard "California National Guard"), [United States military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces "United States Armed Forces"), and several federal law enforcement agencies deployed more than 10,000 of their armed responders to assist in ending the violence and unrest.<sup about="#mwt35" id="cite_ref-7" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-7&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-7" id="mwLw"><span id="mwMA"><span id="mwMQ">[</span>6<span id="mwMg">]</span></span></a></sup>

When the riots ended, 55 people had been killed, 11 of them by the police or [National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Guard_(United_States) "National Guard (United States)"),<sup about="#mwt36" id="cite_ref-LASpreadsheet_2-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;LASpreadsheet&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-LASpreadsheet-2" id="mwNQ"><span id="mwNg"><span id="mwNw">[</span>2<span id="mwOA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt39" id="cite_ref-Miranda_8-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Miranda&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Miranda-8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Miranda-8" id="mwOQ"><span id="mwOg"><span id="mwOw">[</span>7<span id="mwPA">]</span></span></a></sup> 2,383 had been injured, more than 12,000 had been arrested, and estimates of property damage were over $1 billion, making it the most destructive period of local unrest in US history. [Koreatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koreatown,_Los_Angeles "Koreatown, Los Angeles"), situated just to the north of South Central LA, was disproportionately damaged because of racial tensions between the Black and Korean communities. Much of the blame for the extensive nature of the violence was attributed to LAPD chief of police [Daryl Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Gates "Daryl Gates"), who had already announced his resignation by the time of the riots, for failure to de-escalate the situation and overall mismanagement.<sup about="#mwt42" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-9&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-9" id="mwPw"><span id="mwQA"><span id="mwQQ">[</span>8<span id="mwQg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt45" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-10&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-10" id="mwQw"><span id="mwRA"><span id="mwRQ">[</span>9<span id="mwRg">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:South_Central_Los_Angeles_1.jpg)

[South Central Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Los_Angeles "South Los Angeles"), where much of the rioting took place<sup about="#mwt46" id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_11-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ReferenceA&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ReferenceA-11&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-ReferenceA-11" id="mwTg"><span id="mwTw"><span id="mwUA">[</span>10<span id="mwUQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

Before the release of the [Rodney King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_King "Rodney King") videotape, [minority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minority_group "Minority group") community leaders in Los Angeles had repeatedly complained about harassment and use of excessive force against their residents by [Los Angeles Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Police_Department "Los Angeles Police Department") (LAPD) officers.<sup about="#mwt49" id="cite_ref-ReinholdReport_12-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ReinholdReport&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-ReinholdReport-12&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-ReinholdReport-12" id="mwVw"><span id="mwWA"><span id="mwWQ">[</span>11<span id="mwWg">]</span></span></a></sup> [Daryl Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Gates "Daryl Gates"), Chief of the LAPD from 1978 to 1992, has been blamed for the riots.<sup about="#mwt52" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-13&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-13" id="mwXA"><span id="mwXQ"><span id="mwXg">[</span>12<span id="mwXw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt55" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-14&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-14" id="mwYA"><span id="mwYQ"><span id="mwYg">[</span>13<span id="mwYw">]</span></span></a></sup> According to one study, "scandalous racist violence... marked the LAPD under Gates' tempestuous leadership."<sup about="#mwt58" id="cite_ref-15" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-15&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-15" id="mwZA"><span id="mwZQ"><span id="mwZg">[</span>14<span id="mwZw">]</span></span></a></sup> Under Gates, the LAPD had begun [Operation Hammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Hammer_(1987) "Operation Hammer (1987)") in April 1987, which was a large-scale militarized push in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles").

The city, like other large metropolitan areas in United States, was also largely affected by a wave of crime due to the [crack epidemic in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crack_epidemic_in_the_United_States "Crack epidemic in the United States"), the [Crips–Bloods gang war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crips%E2%80%93Bloods_gang_war "Crips–Bloods gang war") and an intensification of the [war on drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_drugs "War on drugs").

The origin of Operation Hammer can be traced to the [1984 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics "1984 Summer Olympics") held in Los Angeles. Under Gates' direction, the LAPD expanded gang sweeps for the duration of the Olympics. These were implemented across wide areas of the city but especially in South Central and East Los Angeles, areas of predominantly minority residents. After the games were over, the city began to revive the use of earlier anti-[trade union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_union "Trade union") and anti-[syndicalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicalism "Syndicalism") laws in order to maintain the security policy started for the Olympic games. The police more frequently conducted mass arrests of [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American") youth. Citizen complaints against [police brutality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_brutality "Police brutality") increased 33 percent in the period 1984–1989.<sup about="#mwt61" id="cite_ref-16" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-16&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-16" id="mwdA"><span id="mwdQ"><span id="mwdg">[</span>15<span id="mwdw">]</span></span></a></sup>

By 1990 over 50,000 people, mostly minority males, had been arrested in such raids.<sup about="#mwt64" id="cite_ref-17" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-17&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-17" id="mweQ"><span id="mweg"><span id="mwew">[</span>16<span id="mwfA">]</span></span></a></sup> Critics have stated that the operation was racially motivated because it used [racial profiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_profiling "Racial profiling"), targeting African American and [Mexican American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_American "Mexican American") youths.<sup about="#mwt67" id="cite_ref-18" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-18&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-18" id="mwfw"><span id="mwgA"><span id="mwgQ">[</span>17<span id="mwgg">]</span></span></a></sup> The perception that police had targeted non-white citizens likely contributed to the anger that erupted in the 1992 riots.<sup about="#mwt70" id="cite_ref-19" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-19&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-19" id="mwgw"><span id="mwhA"><span id="mwhQ">[</span>18<span id="mwhg">]</span></span></a></sup>

The [Christopher Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Commission "Christopher Commission") later concluded that a "significant number" of LAPD officers "repetitively use excessive force against the public and persistently ignore the written guidelines of the department regarding force". The biases related to race, gender, and sexual orientation were found to have regularly contributed to the LAPD's use of excessive force.<sup about="#mwt71" id="cite_ref-Reinhold_20-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Reinhold&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Reinhold-20" id="mwiQ"><span id="mwig"><span id="mwiw">[</span>19<span id="mwjA">]</span></span></a></sup> The commission's report called for the replacement of both Chief [Daryl Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Gates "Daryl Gates") and the civilian [Police Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Board_of_Police_Commissioners "Los Angeles Board of Police Commissioners").<sup about="#mwt72" id="cite_ref-Reinhold_20-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Reinhold&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Reinhold-20" id="mwjw"><span id="mwkA"><span id="mwkQ">[</span>19<span id="mwkg">]</span></span></a></sup>

In the years before the riots, resentment and violence between the African American and Korean American communities in Los Angeles were increasing.<sup about="#mwt77" id="cite_ref-21" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-21&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-21" id="mwlw"><span id="mwmA"><span id="mwmQ">[</span>20<span id="mwmg">]</span></span></a></sup> Many Korean shopkeepers were upset because they suspected shoplifting from their black customers and neighbors. Many black customers were angry because they routinely felt disrespected and humiliated by Korean store owners. Neither group fully understood the extent of the cultural differences and language barriers, which further fueled tensions.<sup about="#mwt80" id="cite_ref-22" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-22&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-22" id="mwmw"><span id="mwnA"><span id="mwnQ">[</span>21<span id="mwng">]</span></span></a></sup>

On March 16, 1991, a year before the Los Angeles riots, storekeeper Soon Ja Du shot and killed Black ninth-grader [Latasha Harlins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Latasha_Harlins "Killing of Latasha Harlins") after a physical altercation. Du was convicted of voluntary manslaughter and the jury recommended the maximum sentence of 16 years, but the judge, [Joyce Karlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joyce_Karlin "Joyce Karlin"), decided against prison time and sentenced Du to five years of probation, 400 hours of community service, and a $500 fine instead.<sup about="#mwt83" id="cite_ref-23" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-23&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-23" id="mwog"><span id="mwow"><span id="mwpA">[</span>22<span id="mwpQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Relations between the African American and Korean communities significantly worsened after this, and the former became increasingly mistrustful of the criminal justice system.<sup about="#mwt86" id="cite_ref-24" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-24&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-24" id="mwpg"><span id="mwpw"><span id="mwqA">[</span>23<span id="mwqQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

Tensions between African Americans and Korean American store owners in South Central Los Angeles were already signaled in the 1991 [Ice Cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Cube "Ice Cube") song "Black Korea."<sup about="#mwt89" id="cite_ref-25" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-25&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-25" id="mwrA"><span id="mwrQ"><span id="mwrg">[</span>24<span id="mwrw">]</span></span></a></sup> The _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ reported on several other significant incidents of violence between the communities at the time:

> Other recent incidents involve the tragic events of May 25, 1991, where two employees at a liquor store near 35th Street and Central Avenue were shot. Both victims, who had recently immigrated from Korea, lost their lives after complying with the demands of a robber described by the police as an African American. Additionally, last Thursday, an African American man suspected of committing a robbery in an auto parts store on Manchester Avenue was fatally injured by his accomplice. The incident occurred when his accomplice accidentally discharged a shotgun round during a struggle with the Korean American owner of the shop. "This violence is deeply unsettling," stated store owner Park. "But sadly, who speaks up for these victims?"<sup about="#mwt92" id="cite_ref-26" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-26&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-26" id="mwtA"><span id="mwtQ"><span id="mwtg">[</span>25<span id="mwtw">]</span></span></a></sup>

Legal scholar Alice H. Choi saw four "prominent factors" that led to the riots: "(a) racism; (b) tension among ethnic minorities; (c) economic strife in the African American community juxtaposed against the apparent success of Korean Americans doing business in the community; and, (d) exploitation of all of the above by the media." She sees the interaction between Du and Harlins as an example of how different cultural systems can clash: "It is possible that Du, being the older woman, expected courtesy from Harlins, a teenager, and Harlins, as a customer, expected the same courtesy from Du, a merchant."<sup about="#mwt95" id="cite_ref-27" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-27&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-27" id="mwuQ"><span id="mwug"><span id="mwuw">[</span>26<span id="mwvA">]</span></span></a></sup>

On the evening of March 3, 1991, Rodney King and two passengers were driving west on the [Foothill Freeway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_210_and_State_Route_210_(California) "Interstate 210 and State Route 210 (California)") (I-210) through the [Sunland-Tujunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunland-Tujunga,_Los_Angeles "Sunland-Tujunga, Los Angeles") neighborhood of the [San Fernando Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Fernando_Valley "San Fernando Valley").<sup about="#mwt101" id="cite_ref-28" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-28&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-28" id="mwxA"><span id="mwxQ"><span id="mwxg">[</span>27<span id="mwxw">]</span></span></a></sup> The [California Highway Patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Highway_Patrol "California Highway Patrol") (CHP) attempted to initiate a [traffic stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_stop "Traffic stop") and a high-speed pursuit ensued with speeds estimated at up to 115 mph (185 km/h), before King eventually exited the freeway at Foothill Boulevard. The pursuit continued through residential neighborhoods of [Lake View Terrace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_View_Terrace "Lake View Terrace") in San Fernando Valley before King stopped in front of the [Hansen Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hansen_Dam "Hansen Dam") recreation center. When King finally stopped, LAPD and CHP officers surrounded King's vehicle and married CHP officers Timothy and Melanie Singer arrested him and the other occupants.<sup about="#mwt104" id="cite_ref-query.nytimes.com_29-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;query.nytimes.com&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-query.nytimes.com-29&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-query.nytimes.com-29" id="mwzQ"><span id="mwzg"><span id="mwzw">[</span>28<span id="mw0A">]</span></span></a></sup>

After the two passengers were placed in the patrol car, five [Los Angeles Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Police_Department "Los Angeles Police Department") (LAPD) officers – [Stacey Koon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stacey_Koon "Stacey Koon"), Laurence Powell, Timothy Wind, Theodore Briseno, and Rolando Solano – surrounded King, who came out of the car last. None of the officers involved were African-American; officers Koon, Wind and Powell were [white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Americans "White Americans"), while Briseno and Solano were of [Hispanic origin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_and_Latino_Americans "Hispanic and Latino Americans").<sup about="#mwt107" id="cite_ref-30" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-30&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-30" id="mw1g"><span id="mw1w"><span id="mw2A">[</span>29<span id="mw2Q">]</span></span></a></sup> They [tasered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroshock_gun "Electroshock gun") King, struck him dozens of times with side-handled batons, kick-stomped him in his back and tackled him to the ground before handcuffing him and hogtying his legs. Sergeant Koon later testified at trial that King resisted arrest and that he believed King was under the influence of [PCP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phencyclidine "Phencyclidine") at the time of the arrest, causing him to be aggressive and violent toward the officers.<sup about="#mwt110" id="cite_ref-31" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-31&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-31" id="mw3A"><span id="mw3Q"><span id="mw3g">[</span>30<span id="mw3w">]</span></span></a></sup> Video footage of the arrest showed that King attempted to get up each time he was struck and that the police made no attempt to cuff him until he lay still.<sup about="#mwt113" id="cite_ref-YouTubeNewsBeatingVideo_32-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;YouTubeNewsBeatingVideo&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-YouTubeNewsBeatingVideo-32&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-YouTubeNewsBeatingVideo-32" id="mw4A"><span id="mw4Q"><span id="mw4g">[</span>31<span id="mw4w">]</span></span></a></sup> A subsequent test of King for the presence of PCP in his body at the time of the arrest was negative.<sup about="#mwt116" id="cite_ref-33" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-33&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-33" id="mw5A"><span id="mw5Q"><span id="mw5g">[</span>32<span id="mw5w">]</span></span></a></sup>

Unbeknownst to the police and King, the incident was captured on a camcorder by local civilian George Holliday from his nearby apartment across from Hansen Dam. The tape was roughly 12 minutes long. While the tape was presented during the trial, some clips of the incident were not released to the public.<sup about="#mwt120" id="cite_ref-NYDailyHolliday_34-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYDailyHolliday&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NYDailyHolliday-34&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYDailyHolliday-34" id="mw6Q"><span id="mw6g"><span id="mw6w">[</span>33<span id="mw7A">]</span></span></a></sup> In a later interview, King, who was on [parole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parole "Parole") for a robbery conviction and had past convictions for assault, battery and robbery,<sup about="#mwt123" id="cite_ref-35" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-35&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-35" id="mw7g"><span id="mw7w"><span id="mw8A">[</span>34<span id="mw8Q">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt126" id="cite_ref-36" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-36&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-36" id="mw8g"><span id="mw8w"><span id="mw9A">[</span>35<span id="mw9Q">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt117" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mw9g" data-mw="{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Reference page&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Reference_page&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;pages&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;41–42&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><span title="Pages: 41–42"><span typeof="mw:Entity">:</span><span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span>41–42<span typeof="mw:Entity"> </span></span></sup>  said he did not surrender earlier because he was driving while intoxicated, which he knew violated the terms of his parole.

The footage of King being beaten by police became an instant focus of media attention and a rallying point for activists in Los Angeles and around the United States. Coverage was extensive during the first two weeks after the incident: the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ published 43 articles about it,<sup about="#mwt129" id="cite_ref-37" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-37&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-37" id="mw-g"><span id="mw-w"><span id="mw_A">[</span>36<span id="mw_Q">]</span></span></a></sup> _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ published 17 articles,<sup about="#mwt133" id="cite_ref-38" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-38&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-38" id="mwAQA"><span id="mwAQE"><span id="mwAQI">[</span>37<span id="mwAQM">]</span></span></a></sup> and the _[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")_ published 11 articles.<sup about="#mwt136" id="cite_ref-39" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-39&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-39" id="mwAQY"><span id="mwAQc"><span id="mwAQg">[</span>38<span id="mwAQk">]</span></span></a></sup> Eight stories appeared on [ABC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)"), including a 60-minute special on _[Primetime Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Live "Primetime Live")._<sup about="#mwt139" id="cite_ref-40" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-40&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-40" id="mwAQ0"><span id="mwAQ4"><span id="mwAQ8">[</span>39<span id="mwARA">]</span></span></a></sup>

Upon watching the tape of the beating, LAPD chief of police [Daryl Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Gates "Daryl Gates") said:

> I stared at the screen in disbelief. I played the one-minute-50-second tape again. Then again and again, until I had viewed it 25 times. And still I could not believe what I was looking at. To see my officers engage in what appeared to be excessive use of force, possibly criminally excessive, to see them beat a man with their batons 56 times, to see a sergeant on the scene who did nothing to seize control, was something I never dreamed I would witness.<sup about="#mwt142" id="cite_ref-41" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-41&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-41" id="mwARU"><span id="mwARY"><span id="mwARc">[</span>40<span id="mwARg">]</span></span></a></sup>

The [Los Angeles County District Attorney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_District_Attorney "Los Angeles County District Attorney") charged four police officers, including one sergeant, with assault and use of excessive force.<sup about="#mwt146" id="cite_ref-NYT_19920306_42-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYT_19920306&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NYT_19920306-42&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYT_19920306-42" id="mwARw"><span id="mwAR0"><span id="mwAR4">[</span>41<span id="mwAR8">]</span></span></a></sup> Due to the extensive media coverage of the arrest, the trial received a [change of venue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Change_of_venue "Change of venue") from [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County "Los Angeles County") to [Simi Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simi_Valley "Simi Valley") in neighboring [Ventura County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura_County,_California "Ventura County, California").<sup about="#mwt149" id="cite_ref-43" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-43&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-43" id="mwASQ"><span id="mwASU"><span id="mwASY">[</span>42<span id="mwASc">]</span></span></a></sup> The jury had no members who were entirely African American.<sup about="#mwt152" id="cite_ref-44" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-44&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-44" id="mwASg"><span id="mwASk"><span id="mwASo">[</span>43<span id="mwASs">]</span></span></a></sup> The jury was composed of nine white Americans (three women, six men), one biracial man,<sup about="#mwt155" id="cite_ref-laist_20120428_45-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;laist_20120428&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-laist_20120428-45&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-laist_20120428-45" id="mwASw"><span id="mwAS0"><span id="mwAS4">[</span>44<span id="mwAS8">]</span></span></a></sup> one Latin American woman, and one [Asian-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_American "Asian American") woman.<sup about="#mwt158" id="cite_ref-NYT_19920506_46-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYT_19920506&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NYT_19920506-46&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYT_19920506-46" id="mwATE"><span id="mwATI"><span id="mwATM">[</span>45<span id="mwATQ">]</span></span></a></sup> The prosecutor, Terry White, was Black.<sup about="#mwt161" id="cite_ref-47" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-47&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-47" id="mwATU"><span id="mwATY"><span id="mwATc">[</span>46<span id="mwATg">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt163" id="cite_ref-48" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-48&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-48" id="mwATk"><span id="mwATo"><span id="mwATs">[</span>47<span id="mwATw">]</span></span></a></sup>

On April 29, 1992, the seventh day of jury deliberations, the jury acquitted all four officers of assault and acquitted three of the four of using excessive force. The jury could not agree on a verdict for the fourth officer charged with using excessive force.<sup about="#mwt164" id="cite_ref-NYT_19920506_46-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYT_19920506&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYT_19920506-46" id="mwAT4"><span id="mwAT8"><span id="mwAUA">[</span>45<span id="mwAUE">]</span></span></a></sup> The verdicts were based in part on the first three seconds of a blurry, 13-second segment of the videotape that, according to journalist [Lou Cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Cannon "Lou Cannon"), had not been aired by television news stations in their broadcasts.<sup about="#mwt167" id="cite_ref-49" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-49&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-49" id="mwAUM"><span id="mwAUQ"><span id="mwAUU">[</span>48<span id="mwAUY">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt170" id="cite_ref-50" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-50&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-50" id="mwAUc"><span id="mwAUg"><span id="mwAUk">[</span>49<span id="mwAUo">]</span></span></a></sup>

Afterward, the prosecution suggested that the jurors may have acquitted the officers due to them becoming desensitized to the beating's violence, as the defense played the videotape repeatedly in slow motion, breaking it down until its emotional impact was lost.<sup about="#mwt171" id="cite_ref-:3_51-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:3&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:3-51" id="mwAUw"><span id="mwAU0"><span id="mwAU4">[</span>50<span id="mwAU8">]</span></span></a></sup>

Outside the Simi Valley courthouse where the acquittals were delivered, county sheriff's deputies protected Stacey Koon from angry protesters on the way to his car. Movie director [John Singleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Singleton "John Singleton"), who was in the crowd at the courthouse, predicted, "By having this verdict, what these people done, they lit the fuse to a bomb."<sup about="#mwt172" id="cite_ref-52" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-52&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-52" id="mwAVI"><span id="mwAVM"><span id="mwAVQ">[</span>51<span id="mwAVU">]</span></span></a></sup>

The riots began the day the verdicts were announced and peaked in intensity over the next two days. A dusk-to-dawn [curfew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curfew "Curfew") and deployment by the [California National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_National_Guard "California National Guard"), [US troops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces "United States Armed Forces"), and [federal law enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_law_enforcement_in_the_United_States "Federal law enforcement in the United States") personnel eventually controlled the situation.<sup about="#mwt175" id="cite_ref-cnn_fast_fact_53-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;cnn fast fact&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-cnn_fast_fact-53&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-cnn_fast_fact-53" id="mwAVw"><span id="mwAV0"><span id="mwAV4">[</span>52<span id="mwAV8">]</span></span></a></sup>

A total of 63 people died during the riots, including nine shot by police and one by the National Guard.<sup about="#mwt178" id="cite_ref-LA_54-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;LA&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-LA-54&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-LA-54" id="mwAWE"><span id="mwAWI"><span id="mwAWM">[</span>53<span id="mwAWQ">]</span></span></a></sup> Of those killed during the riots, 2 were Asian, 28 were Black, 19 were Latino, and 14 were white. No law enforcement officials died during the riots.<sup about="#mwt181" id="cite_ref-55" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-55&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-55" id="mwAWU"><span id="mwAWY"><span id="mwAWc">[</span>54<span id="mwAWg">]</span></span></a></sup> As many as 2,383 people were reported injured.<sup about="#mwt184" id="cite_ref-UCLA_56-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;UCLA&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-UCLA-56&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-UCLA-56" id="mwAWk"><span id="mwAWo"><span id="mwAWs">[</span>55<span id="mwAWw">]</span></span></a></sup> Estimates of the material losses vary between about $800 million and $1 billion.<sup about="#mwt187" id="cite_ref-TIME_57-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;TIME&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-TIME-57&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-TIME-57" id="mwAW0"><span id="mwAW4"><span id="mwAW8">[</span>56<span id="mwAXA">]</span></span></a></sup> Approximately 3,600 fires were set, destroying 1,100 buildings, with fire calls coming once every minute at some points. Widespread looting also occurred. Rioters targeted stores owned by Koreans and other ethnic Asians, reflecting tensions between them and the African American communities.<sup about="#mwt190" id="cite_ref-CSMDarkest_58-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;CSMDarkest&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-CSMDarkest-58&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-CSMDarkest-58" id="mwAXE"><span id="mwAXI"><span id="mwAXM">[</span>57<span id="mwAXQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

Many of the disturbances were concentrated in [South Central Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Los_Angeles "South Los Angeles"), where the population was majority African American and Latino. Fewer than half of all the riot arrests and a third of those killed during the violence were Latino.<sup about="#mwt193" id="cite_ref-Pastor_59-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Pastor&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Pastor-59&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Pastor-59" id="mwAXc"><span id="mwAXg"><span id="mwAXk">[</span>58<span id="mwAXo">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt194" id="cite_ref-Kwong_60-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kwong&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Kwong-60&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Kwong-60" id="mwAXs"><span id="mwAXw"><span id="mwAX0">[</span>59<span id="mwAX4">]</span></span></a></sup>

The riots caused the [Emergency Broadcast System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_Broadcast_System "Emergency Broadcast System") to be activated on April 30, 1992, on [KCAL-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCAL-TV "KCAL-TV") and KTLA, the first time in the city's history (not counting the test activation).<sup about="#mwt197" id="cite_ref-61" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-61&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-61" id="mwAYI"><span id="mwAYM"><span id="mwAYQ">[</span>60<span id="mwAYU">]</span></span></a></sup>

In the week before the Rodney King verdicts were reached, Los Angeles Police Chief Daryl Gates set aside $1 million for possible police overtime. Even so, on the last day of the trial, two-thirds of the LAPD's patrol captains were out of town in [Ventura, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura,_California "Ventura, California"), on the first day of a three-day training seminar.<sup about="#mwt200" id="cite_ref-:5_62-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:5&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:5-62&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:5-62" id="mwAYo"><span id="mwAYs"><span id="mwAYw">[</span>61<span id="mwAY0">]</span></span></a></sup>

At 1 p.m. on April 29, Judge [Stanley Weisberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Weisberg "Stanley Weisberg") announced that the jury had reached its verdict, which would be read in two hours' time. This was done to allow reporters and police and other emergency responders to prepare for the outcome, as unrest was feared if the officers were acquitted.<sup about="#mwt201" id="cite_ref-:5_62-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:5&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:5-62" id="mwAZA"><span id="mwAZE"><span id="mwAZI">[</span>61<span id="mwAZM">]</span></span></a></sup> The LAPD had activated its Emergency Operations Center, which the Webster Commission described as "the doors were opened, the lights turned on and the coffee pot plugged in", but taken no other preparatory action. Specifically, the people intended to staff that Center were not gathered until 4:45 p.m. In addition, no action was taken to retain extra personnel at the LAPD's shift change at 3 p.m., as the risk of trouble was deemed low.<sup about="#mwt202" id="cite_ref-:5_62-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:5&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:5-62" id="mwAZU"><span id="mwAZY"><span id="mwAZc">[</span>61<span id="mwAZg">]</span></span></a></sup>

The acquittals of the four accused Los Angeles Police Department officers came at 3:15 p.m. local time. By 3:45 p.m., a crowd of more than 300 people had appeared at the Los Angeles County Courthouse protesting the verdicts.<sup about="#mwt203" id="mwAZ4"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

Meanwhile, at approximately 4:15–4:20 p.m., a group of people approached the Pay-Less Liquor and Deli on Florence Avenue just west of Normandie in South Central. In an interview, a member of the group said that the group "just decided they weren't going to pay for what they were getting". The store owner's son was hit with a beer bottle, and two other youths smashed the store's glass front door. Two officers from the 77th Street Division of the LAPD responded to this incident and, finding that the instigators had already left, completed a report.<sup about="#mwt204" id="cite_ref-:0_63-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:0&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:0-63" id="mwAaE"><span id="mwAaI"><span id="mwAaM">[</span>62<span id="mwAaQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt208" id="cite_ref-:1_64-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:1-64&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:1-64" id="mwAaU"><span id="mwAaY"><span id="mwAac">[</span>63<span id="mwAag">]</span></span></a></sup>

At 4:58 p.m.,<sup about="#mwt211" id="cite_ref-65" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-65&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-65" id="mwAaw"><span id="mwAa0"><span id="mwAa4">[</span>64<span id="mwAa8">]</span></span></a></sup> [Los Angeles Mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Los_Angeles "Mayor of Los Angeles") [Tom Bradley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Bradley_(American_politician) "Tom Bradley (American politician)") held a news conference to discuss the verdicts. He both expressed anger about the verdicts and appealed for calm.<sup about="#mwt214" id="cite_ref-:3_51-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:3&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:3-51&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:3-51" id="mwAbI"><span id="mwAbM"><span id="mwAbQ">[</span>50<span id="mwAbU">]</span></span></a></sup>

> Today, this jury told the world that what we all saw with our own eyes wasn't a crime. Today, that jury asked us to accept the senseless and brutal beating of a helpless man. Today, that jury said we should tolerate such conduct by those sworn to protect and serve. My friends, I am here to tell this jury, "No. No, our eyes did not deceive us. We saw what we saw, what we saw was a crime..." We must not endanger the reforms we have achieved by resorting to mindless acts. We must not push back progress by striking back blindly.

— Los Angeles Mayor Tom Bradley, post-verdict press conference

Assistant Los Angeles police chief Bob Vernon later said he believed Bradley's remarks incited a riot and were perhaps taken as a signal by some citizens. Vernon said that the number of police incidents rose in the hour after the mayor's press conference.<sup about="#mwt217" id="cite_ref-:3_51-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:3&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:3-51" id="mwAbk"><span id="mwAbo"><span id="mwAbs">[</span>50<span id="mwAbw">]</span></span></a></sup>

At Florence and Halldale, two officers issued a plea for assistance in apprehending a young suspect who had thrown an object at their car and whom they were pursuing on foot.<sup about="#mwt220" id="cite_ref-lapd.com_66-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;lapd.com&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-lapd.com-66&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-lapd.com-66" id="mwAb8"><span id="mwAcA"><span id="mwAcE">[</span>65<span id="mwAcI">]</span></span></a></sup> Approximately two dozen officers, commanded by 77th Street Division LAPD Lieutenant Michael Moulin, arrived and arrested the youth, 16-year old Seandel Daniels, forcing him into the back of a car. The rough handling of the young man, a well-known minor in the community, further agitated an uneasy and growing crowd, who began taunting and berating the police.<sup about="#mwt223" id="cite_ref-67" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-67&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-67" id="mwAcM"><span id="mwAcQ"><span id="mwAcU">[</span>66<span id="mwAcY">]</span></span></a></sup> Among the crowd were Bart Bartholomew, a white freelance photographer for _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_, and Timothy Goldman, a Black US Air Force veteran<sup about="#mwt226" id="cite_ref-:10_68-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:10&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:10-68&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:10-68" id="mwAck"><span id="mwAco"><span id="mwAcs">[</span>67<span id="mwAcw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt229" id="cite_ref-69" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-69&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-69" id="mwAc0"><span id="mwAc4"><span id="mwAc8">[</span>68<span id="mwAdA">]</span></span></a></sup> who began to record the events with his personal camcorder.<sup about="#mwt232" id="cite_ref-70" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-70&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-70" id="mwAdE"><span id="mwAdI"><span id="mwAdM">[</span>69<span id="mwAdQ">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt233" id="cite_ref-:10_68-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:10&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:10-68" id="mwAdU"><span id="mwAdY"><span id="mwAdc">[</span>67<span id="mwAdg">]</span></span></a></sup>

The police formed a perimeter around the arresting officers as the crowd grew more hostile, leading to further altercations and arrests (including that of [Damian Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Reginald_Denny "Attack on Reginald Denny")' older brother, Mark Jackson). One member of the crowd stole the flashlight of an LAPD officer. Fearing police would resort to [deadly force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadly_force "Deadly force") to repel the growing crowd, Lieutenant Moulin ordered officers out of the area altogether. Moulin later said that officers on the scene were outnumbered and unprepared to handle the situation because their riot equipment was stored at the police academy.<sup about="#mwt234" id="mwAd0"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (July 2020)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

> Hey, forget the flashlight, it's not worth it. It ain't worth it. It's not worth it. Forget the flashlight. Not worth it. Let's go.

— Lieutenant Michael Moulin, bullhorn broadcast as recorded by the Goldman footage at 71st and Normandie<sup about="#mwt239" id="cite_ref-71" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-71&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-71" id="mwAeA"><span id="mwAeE"><span id="mwAeI">[</span>70<span id="mwAeM">]</span></span></a></sup>

Moulin made the call for reporting officers to retreat from the 71st and Normandie area entirely at approximately 5:50 p.m.<sup about="#mwt242" id="cite_ref-ReferenceA_11-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ReferenceA&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-ReferenceA-11" id="mwAeY"><span id="mwAec"><span id="mwAeg">[</span>10<span id="mwAek">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt245" id="cite_ref-:0_63-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:0&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:0-63&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:0-63" id="mwAeo"><span id="mwAes"><span id="mwAew">[</span>62<span id="mwAe0">]</span></span></a></sup> They were sent to an [RTD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_California_Rapid_Transit_District "Southern California Rapid Transit District") bus depot at 54th and Arlington<sup about="#mwt248" id="cite_ref-:7_72-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:7&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:7-72&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:7-72" id="mwAe8"><span id="mwAfA"><span id="mwAfE">[</span>71<span id="mwAfI">]</span></span></a></sup> and told to await further instructions. The command post formed at this location was set up at approximately 6 p.m, but had no cell phones or computers other than those in squad cars. It had insufficient numbers of telephone lines and handheld police radios to assess and respond to the situation.<sup about="#mwt249" id="cite_ref-:7_72-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:7&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:7-72" id="mwAfM"><span id="mwAfQ"><span id="mwAfU">[</span>71<span id="mwAfY">]</span></span></a></sup> Finally, the site had no televisions, which meant that as live broadcasts of unrest began, command post officers could not see any of the coverage.<sup about="#mwt250" id="cite_ref-:8_73-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:8-73" id="mwAfc"><span id="mwAfg"><span id="mwAfk">[</span>72<span id="mwAfo">]</span></span></a></sup>

After the retreat of officers at 71st and Normandie, many proceeded one block south to the intersection of [Florence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Avenue "Florence Avenue") and [Normandie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normandie_Avenue "Normandie Avenue").<sup about="#mwt253" id="cite_ref-74" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-74&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-74" id="mwAf8"><span id="mwAgA"><span id="mwAgE">[</span>73<span id="mwAgI">]</span></span></a></sup> As the crowd began to turn physically dangerous, Bartholomew managed to flee the scene with the help of Goldman. Someone hit Bartholomew with a wood plank, breaking his jaw, while others pounded him and grabbed his camera.<sup about="#mwt254" id="cite_ref-:10_68-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:10&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:10-68" id="mwAgM"><span id="mwAgQ"><span id="mwAgU">[</span>67<span id="mwAgY">]</span></span></a></sup> Just after 6 p.m., a group of young men broke the padlock and windows to Tom's Liquor, allowing a group of more than 100 people to raid the store and loot it.<sup about="#mwt255" id="cite_ref-75" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-75&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-75" id="mwAgc"><span id="mwAgg"><span id="mwAgk">[</span>74<span id="mwAgo">]</span></span></a></sup> Concurrently, the growing number of rioters in the street began attacking civilians who appeared not Black, throwing debris at their cars, pulling them from their vehicles when they stopped, smashing window shops, or assaulting them while they walked on the sidewalks. As Goldman continued to film the scene on the ground with his camcorder, the [Los Angeles News Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_News_Service "Los Angeles News Service") team of Marika Gerrard and [Zoey Tur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoey_Tur "Zoey Tur") arrived in a news helicopter, broadcasting from the air. The LANS feed appeared live on numerous Los Angeles television venues.<sup about="#mwt258" id="cite_ref-76" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-76&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-76" id="mwAg0"><span id="mwAg4"><span id="mwAg8">[</span>75<span id="mwAhA">]</span></span></a></sup>

At approximately 6:15 p.m., as reports of vandalism, looting, and physical attacks continued to come in, Moulin elected to "take the information" but not to respond or send personnel to restore order or rescue people in the area.<sup about="#mwt259" id="cite_ref-lapd.com_66-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;lapd.com&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-lapd.com-66" id="mwAhM"><span id="mwAhQ"><span id="mwAhU">[</span>65<span id="mwAhY">]</span></span></a></sup> Moulin was relieved by a captain, ordered only to assess the Florence and Normandie area, and, again, not to attempt to deploy officers there.<sup about="#mwt262" id="cite_ref-77" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-77&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-77" id="mwAhc"><span id="mwAhg"><span id="mwAhk">[</span>76<span id="mwAho">]</span></span></a></sup> Meanwhile, Tur continued to cover the events in progress live at the intersection. From overhead, Tur described the police presence at the scene around 6:30 p.m. as "none".<sup about="#mwt265" id="cite_ref-merged1_78-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;merged1&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-merged1-78&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-merged1-78" id="mwAhw"><span id="mwAh0"><span id="mwAh4">[</span>77<span id="mwAh8">]</span></span></a></sup>

At 6:43 p.m., a white truck driver, Larry Tarvin, drove down Florence and stopped at a red light at Normandie in a large white [delivery truck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delivery_truck "Delivery truck"). With no radio in his truck, he did not know that he was driving into a riot.<sup about="#mwt268" id="cite_ref-:9_79-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:9&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:9-79&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:9-79" id="mwAiQ"><span id="mwAiU"><span id="mwAiY">[</span>78<span id="mwAic">]</span></span></a></sup> Tarvin was pulled from the vehicle by a group of men including Henry Watson, who proceeded to kick and beat him, before striking him unconscious with a fire extinguisher taken from his own vehicle.<sup about="#mwt271" id="cite_ref-80" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-80&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-80" id="mwAig"><span id="mwAik"><span id="mwAio">[</span>79<span id="mwAis">]</span></span></a></sup> He lay unconscious for more than a minute<sup about="#mwt272" id="cite_ref-merged1_78-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;merged1&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-merged1-78" id="mwAiw"><span id="mwAi0"><span id="mwAi4">[</span>77<span id="mwAi8">]</span></span></a></sup> as his truck was looted, before getting up and staggering back to his vehicle. With the help of an unknown African American, Tarvin drove his truck out of further harm's way.<sup about="#mwt273" id="cite_ref-:9_79-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:9&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:9-79" id="mwAjA"><span id="mwAjE"><span id="mwAjI">[</span>78<span id="mwAjM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt276" id="cite_ref-:8_73-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:8&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:8-73&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:8-73" id="mwAjQ"><span id="mwAjU"><span id="mwAjY">[</span>72<span id="mwAjc">]</span></span></a></sup> Just before he did so, another truck, driven by [Reginald Denny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Reginald_Denny "Attack on Reginald Denny"), entered the intersection.<sup about="#mwt277" id="cite_ref-:9_79-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:9&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:9-79" id="mwAjk"><span id="mwAjo"><span id="mwAjs">[</span>78<span id="mwAjw">]</span></span></a></sup> [United Press International Radio Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Press_International_Radio_Network "United Press International Radio Network") reporter Bob Brill, who was filming the attack on Tarvin, was hit in the head with a bottle and stomped on.<sup about="#mwt280" id="cite_ref-81" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-81&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-81" id="mwAj4"><span id="mwAj8"><span id="mwAkA">[</span>80<span id="mwAkE">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Florence_and_Normandie.jpg)

Looking northeast from the southwestern corner of Florence and Normandie, in March 2010

Reginald Denny, a white construction truck driver, was pulled from his truck and severely beaten by a group of Black men who came to be known as the "LA Four". The attack was recorded on video from Tur's and Gerrard's news helicopter, and broadcast live on US national television. Goldman captured the end of the attack and a close-up of Denny's bloody face.<sup about="#mwt285" id="cite_ref-82" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-82&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-82" id="mwAko"><span id="mwAks"><span id="mwAkw">[</span>81<span id="mwAk0">]</span></span></a></sup> As the LA Four fled, another quartet of Black residents came to Denny's aid, placing him back in his truck, in which one of the rescuers drove him to the hospital. Denny suffered a fractured skull and impairment of his speech and ability to walk, and underwent years of rehabilitative therapy. After unsuccessfully suing the City of Los Angeles, Denny moved to Arizona, where he worked as an independent boat mechanic and has mostly avoided media contact.<sup about="#mwt288" id="cite_ref-83" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-83&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-83" id="mwAk4"><span id="mwAk8"><span id="mwAlA">[</span>82<span id="mwAlE">]</span></span></a></sup>

Around 7:40 p.m., almost an hour after Denny was rescued, another beating was filmed on videotape in that location. Fidel Lopez, a self-employed construction worker and [Guatemalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala"), was pulled from his GMC pickup truck and robbed of $2,000 (equivalent to $4,600 in 2025<sup about="#mwt291" id="cite_ref-inflation-US_84-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Transclusion mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;inflation-US&quot;,&quot;group&quot;:&quot;&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-inflation-US-84&quot;},&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;template&quot;:{&quot;target&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;Inflation/fn&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;./Template:Inflation/fn&quot;},&quot;params&quot;:{&quot;1&quot;:{&quot;wt&quot;:&quot;US&quot;}},&quot;i&quot;:0}}]}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-inflation-US-84" id="mwAlc"><span id="mwAlg"><span id="mwAlk">[</span>83<span id="mwAlo">]</span></span></a></sup>).<sup about="#mwt302" id="cite_ref-85" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-85&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-85" id="mwAls"><span id="mwAlw"><span id="mwAl0">[</span>84<span id="mwAl4">]</span></span></a></sup> Rioters, including [Damian Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Reginald_Denny#The_%22L.A._Four%22 "Attack on Reginald Denny"), smashed his forehead open with a car stereo<sup about="#mwt305" id="cite_ref-nytimes_williams_86-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;nytimes_williams&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-nytimes_williams-86&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-nytimes_williams-86" id="mwAmA"><span id="mwAmE"><span id="mwAmI">[</span>85<span id="mwAmM">]</span></span></a></sup> and one tried to slice his ear off.<sup about="#mwt308" id="cite_ref-:2_87-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:2&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:2-87&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:2-87" id="mwAmQ"><span id="mwAmU"><span id="mwAmY">[</span>86<span id="mwAmc">]</span></span></a></sup> After Lopez lost consciousness, the crowd spray-painted his chest, torso, and genitals black.<sup about="#mwt311" id="cite_ref-88" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-88&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-88" id="mwAmg"><span id="mwAmk"><span id="mwAmo">[</span>87<span id="mwAms">]</span></span></a></sup> He was eventually rescued by Black Reverend Bennie Newton, who told the rioters: "Kill him, and you have to kill me too."<sup about="#mwt312" id="cite_ref-:2_87-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:2&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:2-87" id="mwAmw"><span id="mwAm0"><span id="mwAm4">[</span>86<span id="mwAm8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt315" id="cite_ref-89" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-89&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-89" id="mwAnA"><span id="mwAnE"><span id="mwAnI">[</span>88<span id="mwAnM">]</span></span></a></sup> Lopez survived the attack, but it took him years to fully recover and re-establish his business. Newton and Lopez became close friends.<sup about="#mwt316" id="cite_ref-90" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-90&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-90" id="mwAnQ"><span id="mwAnU"><span id="mwAnY">[</span>89<span id="mwAnc">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1993, Reverend Benny Newton died of leukemia.

Sunset on the first evening of the riots was at 7:36 p.m.<sup about="#mwt321" id="cite_ref-91" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-91&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-91" id="mwAno"><span id="mwAns"><span id="mwAnw">[</span>90<span id="mwAn0">]</span></span></a></sup> The first call reporting a fire came in soon after, at approximately 7:45 p.m.<sup about="#mwt324" id="cite_ref-:6_92-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:6-92&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwAn8"><span id="mwAoA"><span id="mwAoE">[</span>91<span id="mwAoI">]</span></span></a></sup> Police did not return in force to Florence and Normandie until 8:30 p.m.<sup about="#mwt325" id="cite_ref-:1_64-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:1&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:1-64" id="mwAoQ"><span id="mwAoU"><span id="mwAoY">[</span>63<span id="mwAoc">]</span></span></a></sup>

Numerous factors were later blamed for the severity of rioting in the 77th Street Division on the evening of April 29. These included:<sup about="#mwt326" id="cite_ref-:8_73-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:8-73" id="mwAok"><span id="mwAoo"><span id="mwAos">[</span>72<span id="mwAow">]</span></span></a></sup>

-   No effort made to close the busy intersection of Florence and Normandie to traffic.
-   Failure to secure gun stores in the Division (one in particular lost 1,150 guns to looting on April 29).
-   The failure to issue a citywide Tactical Alert until 6:43 p.m., which delayed the arrival of other divisions to assist the 77th.
-   The lack of any response — and in particular, a riot response — to the intersection, which emboldened rioters. Since attacks, looting, and arson were broadcast live, viewers could see that none of these actions were being stopped by police.

As noted, after the verdicts were announced, a crowd of protesters formed at the Los Angeles police headquarters at [Parker Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parker_Center "Parker Center") in [Downtown Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Los_Angeles "Downtown Los Angeles"). The crowd grew as the afternoon passed and became violent. The police formed a [skirmish line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skirmish_line "Skirmish line") to protect the building, sometimes moving back in the headquarters as protesters advanced, attempting to set the Parker Center ablaze.<sup about="#mwt331" id="cite_ref-:4_93-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:4&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:4-93&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:4-93" id="mwApg"><span id="mwApk"><span id="mwApo">[</span>92<span id="mwAps">]</span></span></a></sup> In the midst of this, before 6:30 p.m., police chief Daryl Gates left Parker Center, on his way to the neighborhood of [Brentwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brentwood,_Los_Angeles "Brentwood, Los Angeles").
