There, as the situation in Los Angeles deteriorated, Gates attended a political fundraiser against Los Angeles City Charter Amendment F,<sup about="#mwt332" id="cite_ref-:4_93-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:4&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:4-93" id="mwAp4"><span id="mwAp8"><span id="mwAqA">[</span>92<span id="mwAqE">]</span></span></a></sup> intended to "give City Hall more power over the police chief and provide more civilian review of officer misconduct".<sup about="#mwt335" id="cite_ref-94" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-94&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-94" id="mwAqI"><span id="mwAqM"><span id="mwAqQ">[</span>93<span id="mwAqU">]</span></span></a></sup> The amendment would limit the power and term length of his office.<sup about="#mwt338" id="cite_ref-95" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-95&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-95" id="mwAqY"><span id="mwAqc"><span id="mwAqg">[</span>94<span id="mwAqk">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ANG40InfantryDivisionLosAngelesRiot1992.jpg)

National Guard soldiers patrolling the streets

The Parker Center crowd grew riotous at approximately 9 p.m.,<sup about="#mwt341" id="cite_ref-:6_92-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwAq8"><span id="mwArA"><span id="mwArE">[</span>91<span id="mwArI">]</span></span></a></sup> eventually making their way through the [Civic Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Civic_Center "Los Angeles Civic Center"), attacking law enforcement, overturning vehicles, setting objects ablaze, vandalizing government buildings and blocking traffic on [US Route 101](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_101_in_California "U.S. Route 101 in California") going through other nearby districts in downtown Los Angeles looting and burning stores. Nearby [Los Angeles Fire Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Fire_Department "Los Angeles Fire Department") (LAFD) firefighters were shot at while trying to put out a blaze set by looters. The mayor had requested the [California Army National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Army_National_Guard "California Army National Guard") from [Governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_California "Governor of California") [Pete Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Wilson "Pete Wilson"); the first of these units, the 670th Military Police Company, had traveled almost 300 miles (480 km) from its main armory and arrived in the afternoon to assist local police.<sup about="#mwt340" id="mwArs"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (February 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

In the [Lake View Terrace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_View_Terrace,_Los_Angeles "Lake View Terrace, Los Angeles") district of Los Angeles, 200<sup about="#mwt342" id="cite_ref-:6_92-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwAr8"><span id="mwAsA"><span id="mwAsE">[</span>91<span id="mwAsI">]</span></span></a></sup>–400<sup about="#mwt343" id="cite_ref-:8_73-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:8-73" id="mwAsM"><span id="mwAsQ"><span id="mwAsU">[</span>72<span id="mwAsY">]</span></span></a></sup> protesters gathered about 9:15 p.m. at the site where Rodney King was beaten in 1991, near the Hansen Dam Recreation Area. The group marched south on Osborne Street to the LAPD Foothill Division headquarters.<sup about="#mwt344" id="cite_ref-:6_92-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwAsg"><span id="mwAsk"><span id="mwAso">[</span>91<span id="mwAss">]</span></span></a></sup> There they began rock throwing, shooting into the air, and setting fires. The Foothill division police used riot-breaking techniques to disperse the crowd and arrest those responsible for rock throwing and the fires<sup about="#mwt345" id="cite_ref-:8_73-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:8&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:8-73" id="mwAsw"><span id="mwAs0"><span id="mwAs4">[</span>72<span id="mwAs8">]</span></span></a></sup> eventually leading to rioting and looting in the neighboring area of [Pacoima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacoima,_Los_Angeles "Pacoima, Los Angeles") and its surrounding neighborhoods in the San Fernando Valley.

Mayor Bradley signed an order for a dusk-to-dawn curfew at 12:15 a.m. for the core area affected by the riots, as well as declaring a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") for the city of Los Angeles. At 10:15 a.m., he expanded the area under curfew.<sup about="#mwt346" id="cite_ref-:6_92-4" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwAtY"><span id="mwAtc"><span id="mwAtg">[</span>91<span id="mwAtk">]</span></span></a></sup> By mid-morning, violence appeared widespread and unchecked as extensive [looting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Looting "Looting") and [arson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arson "Arson") were witnessed across [Los Angeles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California "Los Angeles County, California"). Rioting moved from South Central Los Angeles, going north through [Central Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Los_Angeles "Central Los Angeles") causing widespread destruction in the neighborhoods of [Koreatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koreatown,_Los_Angeles "Koreatown, Los Angeles"), [Westlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake,_Los_Angeles "Westlake, Los Angeles"), [Pico-Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pico-Union,_Los_Angeles "Pico-Union, Los Angeles"), [Echo Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echo_Park,_Los_Angeles "Echo Park, Los Angeles"), [Hancock Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock_Park,_Los_Angeles "Hancock Park, Los Angeles"), [Fairfax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairfax_District,_Los_Angeles "Fairfax District, Los Angeles"), [Mid-City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-City,_Los_Angeles "Mid-City, Los Angeles") and [Mid-Wilshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-Wilshire,_Los_Angeles "Mid-Wilshire, Los Angeles") before reaching [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles"). The looting and fires engulfed [Hollywood Boulevard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Boulevard "Hollywood Boulevard"), and simultaneously rioting moved west and south into the neighboring independent cities of [Inglewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California"), [Hawthorne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawthorne,_California "Hawthorne, California"), [Gardena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardena,_California "Gardena, California"), [Compton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compton,_California "Compton, California"), [Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carson,_California "Carson, California") and [Long Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Beach,_California "Long Beach, California"), as well as moving east from South Central Los Angeles into the cities of [Huntington Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Park,_California "Huntington Park, California"), [Walnut Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walnut_Park,_California "Walnut Park, California"), [South Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Gate,_California "South Gate, California") and [Lynwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynwood,_California "Lynwood, California") and [Paramount](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount,_California "Paramount, California"). Looting and vandalism had also gone as far south as Los Angeles regions of the [Harbor Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harbor_Area "Harbor Area") in the neighborhoods of [San Pedro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Pedro,_Los_Angeles "San Pedro, Los Angeles"), [Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_Los_Angeles "Wilmington, Los Angeles"), and [Harbor City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harbor_City,_Los_Angeles "Harbor City, Los Angeles").<sup about="#mwt349" id="cite_ref-96" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-96&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-96" id="mwAvc"><span id="mwAvg"><span id="mwAvk">[</span>95<span id="mwAvo">]</span></span></a></sup>

Koreatown is a roughly 2.7 square-mile (7 square kilometer) neighborhood between Hoover Street and Western Avenue, and 3rd Street and Olympic Boulevard, west of [MacArthur Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacArthur_Park "MacArthur Park") and east of [Hancock Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hancock_Park "Hancock Park")/[Windsor Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Square "Windsor Square").<sup about="#mwt352" id="cite_ref-97" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-97&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-97" id="mwAwA"><span id="mwAwE"><span id="mwAwI">[</span>96<span id="mwAwM">]</span></span></a></sup> Korean immigrants had begun settling in the Mid-Wilshire area in the 1960s after the passage of the [Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_and_Nationality_Act_of_1965 "Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965"). It was here that many opened successful businesses.<sup about="#mwt355" id="cite_ref-98" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-98&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-98" id="mwAwU"><span id="mwAwY"><span id="mwAwc">[</span>97<span id="mwAwg">]</span></span></a></sup>

As the riots spread, the police largely abandoned Koreatown to defend store fronts in the wealthy and predominantly white independent cities of [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills "Beverly Hills") and [West Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Hollywood "West Hollywood").<sup about="#mwt358" id="cite_ref-99" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-99&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-99" id="mwAww"><span id="mwAw0"><span id="mwAw4">[</span>98<span id="mwAw8">]</span></span></a></sup> A Korean American resident later told reporters: "It was containment. The police cut off Koreatown traffic, while we were trapped on the other side without help. Those roads are a gateway to a richer neighborhood. It can't be denied."<sup about="#mwt361" id="cite_ref-CNN_100-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;CNN&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-CNN-100&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-CNN-100" id="mwAxA"><span id="mwAxE"><span id="mwAxI">[</span>99<span id="mwAxM">]</span></span></a></sup> Some Koreans later said they did not expect law enforcement to come to their aid.<sup about="#mwt364" id="cite_ref-photogs_101-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;photogs&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-photogs-101&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-photogs-101" id="mwAxQ"><span id="mwAxU"><span id="mwAxY">[</span>100<span id="mwAxc">]</span></span></a></sup>

The lack of law enforcement forced Koreatown civilians to organize their own armed security teams, mainly composed of store owners, to defend their businesses from rioters.<sup about="#mwt365" id="cite_ref-CNN_100-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;CNN&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-CNN-100" id="mwAxk"><span id="mwAxo"><span id="mwAxs">[</span>99<span id="mwAxw">]</span></span></a></sup> Those who stood on the roof of the California Supermarket at 5th and Western Avenue with firearms were later referred to as the "roof" or "[rooftop Koreans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rooftop_Koreans "Rooftop Koreans")". Many had military experience from serving in the [Republic of Korea Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Korea_Armed_Forces "Republic of Korea Armed Forces") before emigrating to the United States.<sup about="#mwt368" id="cite_ref-102" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-102&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-102" id="mwAx8"><span id="mwAyA"><span id="mwAyE">[</span>101<span id="mwAyI">]</span></span></a></sup> Open gun battles were televised, including an incident in which Korean shopkeepers armed with [M1 carbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M1_carbine "M1 carbine"), [Ruger Mini-14s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruger_Mini-14 "Ruger Mini-14"), pump-action shotguns, and handguns exchanged gunfire with a group of armed looters, and forced their retreat.<sup about="#mwt371" id="cite_ref-103" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-103&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-103" id="mwAyU"><span id="mwAyY"><span id="mwAyc">[</span>102<span id="mwAyg">]</span></span></a></sup> But there were casualties, such as 18-year-old Edward Song Lee, whose body can be seen lying in the street in images taken by [photojournalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photojournalism "Photojournalism") Hyungwon Kang.<sup about="#mwt372" id="cite_ref-photogs_101-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;photogs&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-photogs-101" id="mwAyo"><span id="mwAys"><span id="mwAyw">[</span>100<span id="mwAy0">]</span></span></a></sup>

After events in Koreatown, the [670th MP Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_Military_Police_Brigade_(United_States) "49th Military Police Brigade (United States)") from [National City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_City,_California "National City, California"), California were redeployed to reinforce police patrols guarding the [Korean Cultural Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Cultural_Center,_Los_Angeles "Korean Cultural Center, Los Angeles") and the Consulate-General of South Korea in Los Angeles.<sup about="#mwt375" id="cite_ref-104" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-104&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-104" id="mwAzI"><span id="mwAzM"><span id="mwAzQ">[</span>103<span id="mwAzU">]</span></span></a></sup>

Out of the $850 million worth of damage done in LA, half of it was on Korean-owned businesses.<sup about="#mwt378" id="cite_ref-105" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-105&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-105" id="mwAzc"><span id="mwAzg"><span id="mwAzk">[</span>104<span id="mwAzo">]</span></span></a></sup>

The LAPD and the [Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Sheriff's_Department "Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department") (LASD) organized response began to come together by midday. The LAFD and [Los Angeles County Fire Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_County_Fire_Department "Los Angeles County Fire Department") (LACoFD) began to respond backed by police escort; California Highway Patrol reinforcements were [airlifted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airlift "Airlift") to the city. [US President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") spoke out against the rioting, saying anarchy would not be tolerated. The California Army National Guard, which had been advised not to expect civil disturbance and had, as a result, loaned its riot equipment out to other law enforcement agencies, responded quickly by calling up about 2,000 soldiers, but could not get them to the city until nearly 24 hours had passed. They lacked equipment and had to pick it up from the [JFTB (Joint Forces Training Base), Los Alamitos, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Alamitos_Army_Airfield "Los Alamitos Army Airfield"), which was the location of the California Army Nation Guard's 40th Infantry Division headquarters.<sup about="#mwt381" id="cite_ref-106" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-106&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-106" id="mwA0M"><span id="mwA0Q"><span id="mwA0U">[</span>105<span id="mwA0Y">]</span></span></a></sup>

Air traffic control procedures at Los Angeles International Airport were modified, with all departures and arrivals routed to and from the west, over the Pacific Ocean, avoiding overflights of neighborhoods affected by the rioting.<sup about="#mwt382" id="mwA0k"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

[Bill Cosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cosby "Bill Cosby") spoke on the local television station [KNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNBC "KNBC") and asked people to stop the rioting and watch the [series finale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Series_finale "Series finale") of _[The Cosby Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cosby_Show "The Cosby Show")_.<sup about="#mwt385" id="cite_ref-107" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-107&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-107" id="mwA1A"><span id="mwA1E"><span id="mwA1I">[</span>106<span id="mwA1M">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt389" id="cite_ref-108" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-108&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-108" id="mwA1Q"><span id="mwA1U"><span id="mwA1Y">[</span>107<span id="mwA1c">]</span></span></a></sup> The [US Justice Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice "United States Department of Justice") announced it would resume federal investigation of the Rodney King beating as a violation of federal civil rights law.<sup about="#mwt390" id="cite_ref-:6_92-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwA1k"><span id="mwA1o"><span id="mwA1s">[</span>91<span id="mwA1w">]</span></span></a></sup>

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MT2821_Address_to_the_Nation_Regarding_the_Riots_in_Los_Angeles_-_01_May_1992.webm "Play video")Duration: 12 minutes and 29 seconds.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MT2821_Address_to_the_Nation_Regarding_the_Riots_in_Los_Angeles_-_01_May_1992.webm)

President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") announcing the federalization of the [California Army National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Army_National_Guard "California Army National Guard") and deployment of federal troops to Los Angeles, May 1

In the early morning hours of Friday, May 1, the major rioting was stopped.<sup about="#mwt393" id="cite_ref-La_Riots_Case_Study_1992_109-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;La Riots Case Study 1992&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-La_Riots_Case_Study_1992-109&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-La_Riots_Case_Study_1992-109" id="mwA2g"><span id="mwA2k"><span id="mwA2o">[</span>108<span id="mwA2s">]</span></span></a></sup> Rodney King gave an impromptu news conference in front of his lawyer's office, tearfully saying, "People, I just want to say, you know, can we all get along?"<sup about="#mwt396" id="cite_ref-110" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-110&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-110" id="mwA2w"><span id="mwA20"><span id="mwA24">[</span>109<span id="mwA28">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt399" id="cite_ref-NYT_1993-12-09_111-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYT_1993-12-09&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NYT_1993-12-09-111&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYT_1993-12-09-111" id="mwA3A"><span id="mwA3E"><span id="mwA3I">[</span>110<span id="mwA3M">]</span></span></a></sup> That morning, at 1:00 am, Governor Wilson had requested [federal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") assistance. Upon request, Bush invoked the [Insurrection Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insurrection_Act "Insurrection Act") with [Executive Order 12804](https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Executive%20Order%2012804 "s:Executive Order 12804"), federalizing the California Army National Guard and authorizing [federal troops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces "United States Armed Forces") and [federal law enforcement officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_law_enforcement_in_the_United_States "Federal law enforcement in the United States") to help restore law and order.<sup about="#mwt402" id="cite_ref-LA_Times_112-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;LA Times&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-LA_Times-112&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-LA_Times-112" id="mwA3k"><span id="mwA3o"><span id="mwA3s">[</span>111<span id="mwA3w">]</span></span></a></sup> With Bush's authority, [the Pentagon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pentagon "The Pentagon") activated [Operation Garden Plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Garden_Plot "Operation Garden Plot"), placing the California Army National Guard and federal troops under the newly formed Joint Task Force Los Angeles (JTF-LA).<sup about="#mwt405" id="cite_ref-113" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-113&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-113" id="mwA38"><span id="mwA4A"><span id="mwA4E">[</span>112<span id="mwA4I">]</span></span></a></sup> The deployment of federal troops was not ready until Saturday, by which time the rioting and looting were under control.

Meanwhile, the [40th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40th_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "40th Infantry Division (United States)") (doubled to 4,000 troops) of the California Army National Guard continued to move into the city in [Humvees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humvee "Humvee"); eventually 10,000 Army National Guard troops were activated. That same day, 1,000 federal [tactical officers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_tactical_unit "Police tactical unit") from different agencies across California were dispatched to L.A. to protect federal facilities and assist local police. Later that evening, Bush addressed the country, denouncing "random terror and lawlessness". He summarized his discussions with Mayor Bradley and Governor Wilson and outlined the federal assistance he was making available to local authorities. Citing the "urgent need to restore order", he warned that the "brutality of a mob" would not be tolerated, and he would "use whatever force is necessary". He referred to the Rodney King case, describing talking to his own grandchildren and noting the actions of "good and decent policemen" as well as civil rights leaders. He said he had directed the Justice Department to investigate the King case, and that "grand jury action is underway today", and justice would prevail. The Post Office announced that it was unsafe for their couriers to deliver mail. The public were instructed to pick up their mail at the main Post Office. The lines were approximately 40 blocks long, and the California National Guard were diverted to that location to ensure peace.<sup about="#mwt408" id="cite_ref-114" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-114&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-114" id="mwA4c"><span id="mwA4g"><span id="mwA4k">[</span>113<span id="mwA4o">]</span></span></a></sup>

By this point, many entertainments and sports events were postponed or canceled. The [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_Los_Angeles_Lakers_season "1991–92 Los Angeles Lakers season") hosted the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_Portland_Trail_Blazers_season "1991–92 Portland Trail Blazers season") in an [NBA playoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_NBA_Playoffs "1992 NBA Playoffs") basketball game on the night the rioting started. The following game was postponed until Sunday and moved to [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_&_Mack_Center "Thomas & Mack Center"). The [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_Los_Angeles_Clippers_season "1991–92 Los Angeles Clippers season") moved a playoff game against the [Utah Jazz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_Utah_Jazz_season "1991–92 Utah Jazz season") to nearby [Anaheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim_Convention_Center "Anaheim Convention Center"). In baseball, the Los Angeles Dodgers postponed games for four straight days from Thursday to Sunday, including a whole three-game series against the [Montreal Expos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Montreal_Expos_season "1992 Montreal Expos season"); all were made up as part of [doubleheaders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doubleheader_(baseball) "Doubleheader (baseball)") in July. In San Francisco, a city curfew due to unrest forced the postponement of a May 1, [San Francisco Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_San_Francisco_Giants_season "1992 San Francisco Giants season") home game against the [Philadelphia Phillies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Philadelphia_Phillies_season "1992 Philadelphia Phillies season").<sup about="#mwt411" id="cite_ref-115" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-115&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-115" id="mwA5c"><span id="mwA5g"><span id="mwA5k">[</span>114<span id="mwA5o">]</span></span></a></sup>

The [horse racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_racing "Horse racing") venues [Hollywood Park Racetrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Park_Racetrack "Hollywood Park Racetrack") and [Los Alamitos Race Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Alamitos_Race_Course "Los Alamitos Race Course") were also shut down. LA [Fiesta Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiesta_Broadway "Fiesta Broadway"), a major event in the Latino community, was canceled. In music, [Van Halen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Halen "Van Halen") canceled two concert shows in [Inglewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inglewood,_California "Inglewood, California") on Saturday and Sunday. [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica") and [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses") were forced to postpone and relocate their concert to the [Rose Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Bowl_(stadium) "Rose Bowl (stadium)") as the LA Coliseum and its surrounding neighborhood were still damaged. [Michael Bolton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bolton "Michael Bolton") canceled his scheduled performance at the [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl") Sunday. [The World Wrestling Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE "WWE") canceled events on Friday and Saturday in the cities of [Long Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_Beach,_California "Long Beach, California") and [Fresno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno,_California "Fresno, California").<sup about="#mwt414" id="cite_ref-116" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-116&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-116" id="mwA6o"><span id="mwA6s"><span id="mwA6w">[</span>115<span id="mwA60">]</span></span></a></sup> By the end of Friday night, all the remaining smaller riots were completely quelled.<sup about="#mwt415" id="cite_ref-La_Riots_Case_Study_1992_109-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;La Riots Case Study 1992&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-La_Riots_Case_Study_1992-109" id="mwA64"><span id="mwA68"><span id="mwA7A">[</span>108<span id="mwA7E">]</span></span></a></sup>

On the fourth day, 3,500 federal troops – 2,000 [soldiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") of the [7th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "7th Infantry Division (United States)") from [Fort Ord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Ord "Fort Ord") and 1,500 [Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps") of the [1st Marine Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Marine_Division_(United_States) "1st Marine Division (United States)") from [Camp Pendleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Pendleton "Camp Pendleton") – arrived to reinforce the National Guard soldiers already in the city. The Marine Corps contingent included the [1st Light Armored Reconnaissance Battalion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Light_Armored_Reconnaissance_Battalion "1st Light Armored Reconnaissance Battalion"), commanded by [John F. Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kelly "John F. Kelly"). It was the first significant [military occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_occupation "Military occupation") of Los Angeles by federal troops since the 1894 [Pullman Strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pullman_Strike "Pullman Strike"),<sup about="#mwt419" id="cite_ref-117" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-117&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-117" id="mwA74"><span id="mwA78"><span id="mwA8A">[</span>116<span id="mwA8E">]</span></span></a></sup> and also the first federal military intervention in an American city to quell a civil disorder since the 1968 [King assassination riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_assassination_riots "King assassination riots"), and the deadliest modern unrest since the [1980 Miami riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Miami_riots "1980 Miami riots") at the time, only 12 years earlier.<sup about="#mwt416" id="mwA8U"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (January 2022)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

These federal military forces took 24 hours to deploy to [Huntington Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huntington_Park,_California "Huntington Park, California"), about the same time it took for the National Guard.<sup about="#mwt420" id="mwA8k"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2020)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> This brought total troop strength to 13,500, making LA the largest military occupation of any US city since the [1968 Washington, D.C. riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Washington,_D.C.,_riots "1968 Washington, D.C., riots"). Federal troops joined National Guard soldiers to support local police in restoring order directly; the combined force contributed significantly to preventing violence.<sup about="#mwt421" id="mwA8w"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (April 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup> With most of the violence under control, 30,000 people attended an 11 a.m. peace rally in Koreatown to support local merchants and racial healing.<sup about="#mwt422" id="cite_ref-:6_92-6" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:6&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:6-92" id="mwA80"><span id="mwA84"><span id="mwA88">[</span>91<span id="mwA9A">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Los_Angeles_Riots,_1992_(17094264951).jpg)

Smoke over the city from a distance

Mayor Bradley assured the public that the crisis was, more or less, under control as areas became quiet.<sup about="#mwt425" id="cite_ref-118" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-118&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-118" id="mwA9c"><span id="mwA9g"><span id="mwA9k">[</span>117<span id="mwA9o">]</span></span></a></sup> Later that night, Army National Guard soldiers shot and killed a motorist who tried to run them over at a barrier.<sup about="#mwt428" id="cite_ref-119" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-119&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-119" id="mwA9s"><span id="mwA9w"><span id="mwA90">[</span>118<span id="mwA94">]</span></span></a></sup>

In another incident, the LAPD and Marines intervened in a domestic dispute in Compton, in which the suspect held his wife and children [hostage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hostage "Hostage"). As the officers approached, the suspect fired two shotgun rounds through the door, injuring some of the officers. One of the officers yelled to the Marines, "Cover me", as per law enforcement training to be prepared to fire if necessary. However, per their military training, the Marines interpreted the wording as providing cover by establishing a base of [firepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firepower "Firepower"), resulting in a total of 200 rounds being sprayed into the house. Remarkably, neither the suspect nor the woman and children inside the house were harmed.<sup about="#mwt431" id="cite_ref-120" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-120&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-120" id="mwA-I"><span id="mwA-M"><span id="mwA-Q">[</span>119<span id="mwA-U">]</span></span></a></sup>

Although Mayor Bradley lifted the curfew, signaling the official end of the riots, sporadic violence and crime continued for a few days afterward. Schools, banks, and businesses reopened. Federal troops did not stand down until May 9. The Army National Guard remained until May 14. Some National Guard soldiers remained as late as May 27.<sup about="#mwt434" id="cite_ref-121" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-121&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-121" id="mwA-g"><span id="mwA-k"><span id="mwA-o">[</span>120<span id="mwA-s">]</span></span></a></sup>

Many Korean Americans in Los Angeles refer to the event as 'Sa-I-Gu', meaning "four-two-nine" in the [Korean language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language") (4.29), in reference to April 29, 1992, which was the day the riots started. Over 2,300 [mom-and-pop shops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mom-and-pop_shop "Mom-and-pop shop") run by Korean business owners were damaged through ransacking and looting during the riots, sustaining close to $400 million in damages.<sup about="#mwt439" id="cite_ref-122" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-122&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-122" id="mwA_M"><span id="mwA_Q"><span id="mwA_U">[</span>121<span id="mwA_Y">]</span></span></a></sup>

During the riots, Korean Americans received very little aid or protection from police authorities, due to their low social status and language barriers.<sup about="#mwt442" id="cite_ref-Kim_123-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kim&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Kim-123&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Kim-123" id="mwA_g"><span id="mwA_k"><span id="mwA_o">[</span>122<span id="mwA_s">]</span></span></a></sup> Many Koreans rushed to [Koreatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koreatown,_Los_Angeles "Koreatown, Los Angeles") after Korean-language radio stations called for volunteers to guard against rioters. Many of the volunteers that helped defend the Korean stores were from an organization called LA Korean Youth Task Force and they went to protect these stores because there were no adult males in those families that could do it.<sup about="#mwt445" id="cite_ref-124" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-124&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-124" id="mwA_0"><span id="mwA_4"><span id="mwA_8">[</span>123<span id="mwBAA">]</span></span></a></sup> Many were armed, with a variety of improvised weapons, handguns, shotguns, and [semi-automatic rifles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-automatic_rifle "Semi-automatic rifle").<sup about="#mwt446" id="cite_ref-LA_Times_112-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;LA Times&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-LA_Times-112" id="mwBAI"><span id="mwBAM"><span id="mwBAQ">[</span>111<span id="mwBAU">]</span></span></a></sup>

Television coverage of two Korean merchants firing pistols repeatedly at roving looters was widely seen and controversial. _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")_ said: "that the image seemed to speak of race war, and of vigilantes taking the law into their own hands."<sup about="#mwt449" id="cite_ref-NY_Times2_125-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NY Times2&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NY_Times2-125&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NY_Times2-125" id="mwBAk"><span id="mwBAo"><span id="mwBAs">[</span>124<span id="mwBAw">]</span></span></a></sup> One of the merchants, David Joo, said, "I want to make it clear that we didn't open fire first. At that time, four police cars were there. Somebody started to shoot at us. The LAPD ran away in half a second. I never saw such a fast escape. I was pretty disappointed." Carl Rhyu, also a participant in the Koreans' armed response, said, "If it was your own business and your own property, would you be willing to trust it to someone else? We are glad the National Guard is here. They're good backup. But when our shops were burning we called the police every five minutes; no response."<sup about="#mwt450" id="cite_ref-NY_Times2_125-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NY Times2&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NY_Times2-125" id="mwBA0"><span id="mwBA4"><span id="mwBA8">[</span>124<span id="mwBBA">]</span></span></a></sup> At a shopping center several miles north of Koreatown, Jay Rhee, who said he and others fired five hundred shots into the ground and air, said, "We have lost our faith in the police. Where were you when we needed you?" Despite Koreatown's relative geographical isolation from South Central Los Angeles, it was the most severely damaged in the riots.<sup about="#mwt451" id="cite_ref-Kim_123-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kim&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Kim-123" id="mwBBE"><span id="mwBBI"><span id="mwBBM">[</span>122<span id="mwBBQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

The riots have been considered a major turning point in the development of a distinct Korean American identity and community. Korean Americans responded in various ways, including the development of new ethnic agendas and organization and increased political activism.

One of the largest armed camps in Los Angeles's Koreatown congregated at the California Market. On the first night after the officers' verdicts were returned, Richard Rhee, the market owner, set up camp in the parking lot with about 20 armed employees.<sup about="#mwt454" id="cite_ref-Los_Angeles_Times_126-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Los Angeles Times&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-126&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Los_Angeles_Times-126" id="mwBBg"><span id="mwBBk"><span id="mwBBo">[</span>125<span id="mwBBs">]</span></span></a></sup> One year after the riots, fewer than one in four damaged or destroyed businesses had reopened, according to the survey conducted by the Korean American Inter-Agency Council.<sup about="#mwt457" id="cite_ref-NY_Times_127-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NY Times&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NY_Times-127&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NY_Times-127" id="mwBBw"><span id="mwBB0"><span id="mwBB4">[</span>126<span id="mwBB8">]</span></span></a></sup> According to a _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ survey conducted eleven months after the riots, almost 40 percent of Korean Americans said they were thinking of leaving Los Angeles.<sup about="#mwt460" id="cite_ref-128" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-128&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-128" id="mwBCI"><span id="mwBCM"><span id="mwBCQ">[</span>127<span id="mwBCU">]</span></span></a></sup>

Before a verdict was issued in the new 1993 Rodney King federal civil rights trial against the four officers, many Korean shop owners prepared for violence. Gun sales increased sharply, many to people of Korean descent; some merchants at flea markets removed merchandise from shelves, and they fortified storefronts with extra [Plexiglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plexiglas "Plexiglas") and bars. Throughout the region, merchants readied to defend themselves, and others formed armed militia groups.<sup about="#mwt461" id="cite_ref-NY_Times_127-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NY Times&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NY_Times-127" id="mwBCg"><span id="mwBCk"><span id="mwBCo">[</span>126<span id="mwBCs">]</span></span></a></sup> College student Elizabeth Hwang spoke of the attacks on her parents' convenience store in 1992. She said at the time of the 1993 trial, they had been armed with a [Glock 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glock_17 "Glock 17") pistol, a [Beretta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beretta_M9 "Beretta M9"), and a [shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun "Shotgun"), and they planned to barricade themselves in their store to fight off looters.<sup about="#mwt462" id="cite_ref-NY_Times_127-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NY Times&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NY_Times-127" id="mwBC8"><span id="mwBDA"><span id="mwBDE">[</span>126<span id="mwBDI">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Los_Angeles_Riots,_1992_(17094954065).jpg)

People looting a clothing store

About 2,300 Korean-owned stores in southern California were looted or burned, making up 45 percent of all damages caused by the riot, many of which were uninsured.<sup about="#mwt465" id="cite_ref-:11_129-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:11&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-:11-129&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:11-129" id="mwBDk"><span id="mwBDo"><span id="mwBDs">[</span>128<span id="mwBDw">]</span></span></a></sup> According to the Asian and Pacific American Counseling and Prevention Center, 730 Koreans were treated for [post-traumatic stress disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-traumatic_stress_disorder "Post-traumatic stress disorder"), which included insomnia and a sense of helplessness and muscle pain. In reaction, many Korean Americans worked to create political and social empowerment.<sup about="#mwt466" id="cite_ref-Kim_123-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kim&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Kim-123" id="mwBD4"><span id="mwBD8"><span id="mwBEA">[</span>122<span id="mwBEE">]</span></span></a></sup>

As a result of the LA riots, Korean Americans formed activist organizations such as the Association of Korean American Victims. They built collaborative links with other ethnic groups through groups like the Korean American Coalition.<sup about="#mwt469" id="cite_ref-130" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-130&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-130" id="mwBEM"><span id="mwBEQ"><span id="mwBEU">[</span>129<span id="mwBEY">]</span></span></a></sup> A week after the riots, in the largest Asian American protest ever held in a city, about 30,000 mostly-Korean and Korean American marchers walked the streets of LA Koreatown, calling for peace and denouncing violence. This cultural movement was devoted to the protection of Koreans' political rights, ethnic heritage, and political representation. New leaders arose within the community, and second-generation children spoke on behalf of the community. Korean Americans began to have different occupation goals, from store-owners to political leaders. Korean Americans worked to gain governmental aid to rebuild their damaged neighborhoods. Countless community and advocacy groups have been established to further fuel Korean political representation and understanding.<sup about="#mwt470" id="cite_ref-Kim_123-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kim&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Kim-123" id="mwBEc"><span id="mwBEg"><span id="mwBEk">[</span>122<span id="mwBEo">]</span></span></a></sup>

Edward Taehan Chang, a professor of ethnic studies and founding director of the Young Oak Kim Center for Korean American Studies at the [University of California, Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_California,_Riverside "University of California, Riverside"), has identified the LA riots as a turning point for the development of a Korean American identity separate from that of Korean immigrants and that was more politically active: "They learned a valuable lesson that we have to become much more engaged and politically involved and that political empowerment is very much part of the Korean American future."<sup about="#mwt473" id="cite_ref-131" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-131&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-131" id="mwBE0"><span id="mwBE4"><span id="mwBE8">[</span>130<span id="mwBFA">]</span></span></a></sup>

According to Edward Park, the 1992 violence stimulated a new wave of political activism among Korean Americans, but it also split them into two camps.<sup about="#mwt477" id="cite_ref-132" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-132&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-132" id="mwBFI"><span id="mwBFM"><span id="mwBFQ">[</span>131<span id="mwBFU">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt481" id="cite_ref-133" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-133&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-133" id="mwBFY"><span id="mwBFc"><span id="mwBFg">[</span>132<span id="mwBFk">]</span></span></a></sup> The liberals sought to unite with other minorities in Los Angeles to fight against racial oppression and [scapegoating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapegoating "Scapegoating"). The conservatives emphasized [law and order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_and_order_(politics) "Law and order (politics)") and generally favored the economic and social policies of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"). The conservatives tended to emphasize the differences between Koreans and other minorities, specifically African Americans.<sup about="#mwt482" id="cite_ref-134" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-134&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-134" id="mwBF0"><span id="mwBF4"><span id="mwBF8">[</span>133<span id="mwBGA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt483" id="cite_ref-135" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-135&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-135" id="mwBGE"><span id="mwBGI"><span id="mwBGM">[</span>134<span id="mwBGQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

According to a 1993 report by the Latinos Futures Research Group for the Latino Coalition for a New Los Angeles, one-third of those who were killed and one half of those who were arrested in the riots were Latino (80% of which were recent immigrants);<sup about="#mwt484" id="cite_ref-:11_129-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;:11&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-:11-129" id="mwBGc"><span id="mwBGg"><span id="mwBGk">[</span>128<span id="mwBGo">]</span></span></a></sup> between 20 and 40 percent of the businesses that were looted were owned by Latinos.<sup about="#mwt487" id="cite_ref-Hayes-Bautista_136-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Hayes-Bautista&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Hayes-Bautista-136&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Hayes-Bautista-136" id="mwBGs"><span id="mwBGw"><span id="mwBG0">[</span>135<span id="mwBG4">]</span></span></a></sup> Hispanics were considered a minority despite their increasing numbers, so they lacked political support and were poorly represented. This lack of social and political representation obscured acknowledgment of their participation in the riots. Many who lived in the area were new immigrants, not yet able to speak [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language").<sup about="#mwt490" id="cite_ref-Newman_137-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Newman&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Newman-137&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Newman-137" id="mwBHA"><span id="mwBHE"><span id="mwBHI">[</span>136<span id="mwBHM">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![Many soldiers and military vehicles near a vandalized road sign](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marine_deployment_to_L.A.jpg)

US Marines disembark from their trucks and Humvees in Compton for riot control operations in May 1992; thousands of federal troops patrolled Los Angeles.

Almost as soon as the disturbances broke out in South Central, local television news cameras were on the scene to record the events as they happened.<sup about="#mwt491" id="cite_ref-138" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-138&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-138" id="mwBHo"><span id="mwBHs"><span id="mwBHw">[</span>137<span id="mwBH0">]</span></span></a></sup> Television coverage of the riots was near-continuous, starting with the beating of motorists and pedestrians at the intersection of Florence and Normandie which was broadcast live by television news pilot and reporter [Zoey Tur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoey_Tur "Zoey Tur") and her camera operator Marika Gerrard.<sup about="#mwt494" id="cite_ref-139" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-139&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-139" id="mwBH8"><span id="mwBIA"><span id="mwBIE">[</span>138<span id="mwBII">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt497" id="cite_ref-L.A.TIMES_140-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;L.A.TIMES&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-L.A.TIMES-140&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-L.A.TIMES-140" id="mwBIM"><span id="mwBIQ"><span id="mwBIU">[</span>139<span id="mwBIY">]</span></span></a></sup>

In part because of extensive media coverage of the Los Angeles riots, smaller but similar riots and other anti-police actions took place in other cities throughout the United States.<sup about="#mwt500" id="cite_ref-emergency.com_141-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;emergency.com&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-emergency.com-141&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-emergency.com-141" id="mwBIg"><span id="mwBIk"><span id="mwBIo">[</span>140<span id="mwBIs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt503" id="cite_ref-142" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-142&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-142" id="mwBIw"><span id="mwBI0"><span id="mwBI4">[</span>141<span id="mwBI8">]</span></span></a></sup> The [Emergency Broadcast System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_Broadcast_System "Emergency Broadcast System") was also utilized during the rioting.<sup about="#mwt506" id="cite_ref-143" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-143&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-143" id="mwBJE"><span id="mwBJI"><span id="mwBJM">[</span>142<span id="mwBJQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

On _[Nightline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nightline "Nightline")_, [Ted Koppel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Koppel "Ted Koppel") initially only interviewed Black leaders about the Black/Korean conflict, and they shared detrimental opinions about Korean Americans.<sup about="#mwt509" id="cite_ref-Jump_144-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Jump&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Jump-144&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Jump-144" id="mwBJo"><span id="mwBJs"><span id="mwBJw">[</span>143<span id="mwBJ0">]</span></span></a></sup>

Some felt that too much emphasis was placed on the suffering of Korean Americans. As filmmaker [Dai Sil Kim-Gibson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dai_Sil_Kim-Gibson "Dai Sil Kim-Gibson"), who produced the 1993 documentary _Sa-I-Gu_, described, "black-Korean conflict was one symptom, but it was certainly not the cause of that riot. The cause of that riot was the Black-white conflict that existed in this country from the establishment of this country."<sup about="#mwt512" id="cite_ref-145" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-145&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-145" id="mwBKE"><span id="mwBKI"><span id="mwBKM">[</span>144<span id="mwBKQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

In an [NBC News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_News "NBC News") article, Hanna Kang sees the conflict between Korean and Black Americans as overstated and only part of the story was told in the news. Kang interviewed more than twenty people from both races in many different fields, and all of them had the same view of the media during the riots: they all believe the influence of the news coverage persuaded how the public looked at the riots.<sup about="#mwt513" id="cite_ref-146" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-146&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-146" id="mwBKc"><span id="mwBKg"><span id="mwBKk">[</span>145<span id="mwBKo">]</span></span></a></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LA_Riots_aftermath_-_1991_(149046646).jpg)

Burned buildings in Los Angeles

After the riots subsided, an inquiry was commissioned by the city Police Commission, led by [William H. Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Webster "William H. Webster") (special advisor), and Hubert Williams (deputy special advisor, president of the Police Foundation).<sup about="#mwt517" id="cite_ref-147" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-147&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-147" id="mwBLI"><span id="mwBLM"><span id="mwBLQ">[</span>146<span id="mwBLU">]</span></span></a></sup> The findings of the inquiry, _The City in Crisis: A Report by the Special Advisor to the Board of Police Commissioners on the Civil Disorder in Los Angeles_, also colloquially known as the _Webster Report_ or _Webster Commission_, was released on October 21, 1992.<sup about="#mwt521" id="cite_ref-148" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-148&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-148" id="mwBLk"><span id="mwBLo"><span id="mwBLs">[</span>147<span id="mwBLw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt514" id="mwBL4"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Writing_better_articles#Stay_on_topic" title="Wikipedia:Writing better articles"><span title="The material near this tag may contain information that is not relevant to the article's main topic. (April 2021)">relevant?</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

LAPD chief of police [Daryl Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daryl_Gates "Daryl Gates"), who had seen his successor [Willie L. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_L._Williams "Willie L. Williams") named by the Police Commission days before the riots,<sup about="#mwt524" id="cite_ref-149" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-149&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-149" id="mwBMI"><span id="mwBMM"><span id="mwBMQ">[</span>148<span id="mwBMU">]</span></span></a></sup> was forced to resign on June 28, 1992.<sup about="#mwt527" id="cite_ref-150" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-150&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-150" id="mwBMY"><span id="mwBMc"><span id="mwBMg">[</span>149<span id="mwBMk">]</span></span></a></sup> Some areas of the city saw temporary truces between the rival [Crips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crips "Crips") and [Bloods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloods "Bloods") gangs, as well as between rival Latino gangs, which fueled speculation among LAPD officers that the truce was going to be used to unite the gangs against the department.<sup about="#mwt530" id="cite_ref-151" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-151&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-151" id="mwBMw"><span id="mwBM0"><span id="mwBM4">[</span>150<span id="mwBM8">]</span></span></a></sup>

In addition to the catalyst of the verdicts in the excessive force trial, various other factors have been cited as causes of the unrest, including the death of Latasha Harlins, the young Black girl who was shot by a Korean American shopkeeper in 1991, for which the shooter served no jail time, receiving only five years of probation and 400 hours of community service.<sup about="#mwt533" id="cite_ref-152" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-152&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-152" id="mwBNM"><span id="mwBNQ"><span id="mwBNU">[</span>151<span id="mwBNY">]</span></span></a></sup>

There were other long-term factors for social tensions: high rates of poverty and unemployment among the residents of [South Central Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Central_Los_Angeles "South Central Los Angeles"), which had been deeply affected by the [nationwide recession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late_1980s_recession "Late 1980s recession").<sup about="#mwt536" id="cite_ref-153" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-153&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-153" id="mwBNo"><span id="mwBNs"><span id="mwBNw">[</span>152<span id="mwBN0">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt539" id="cite_ref-154" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-154&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-154" id="mwBN4"><span id="mwBN8"><span id="mwBOA">[</span>153<span id="mwBOE">]</span></span></a></sup> Articles in the _Los Angeles Times_ and _The New York Times_ linked the economic deterioration of South Central to the declining living conditions of the residents, and reported that local resentments about these conditions helped to fuel the riots.<sup about="#mwt542" id="cite_ref-155" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-155&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-155" id="mwBOQ"><span id="mwBOU"><span id="mwBOY">[</span>154<span id="mwBOc">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt543" id="cite_ref-156" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-156&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-156" id="mwBOg"><span id="mwBOk"><span id="mwBOo">[</span>155<span id="mwBOs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt544" id="cite_ref-157" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-157&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-157" id="mwBOw"><span id="mwBO0"><span id="mwBO4">[</span>156<span id="mwBO8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt545" id="cite_ref-158" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-158&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-158" id="mwBPA"><span id="mwBPE"><span id="mwBPI">[</span>157<span id="mwBPM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt546" id="cite_ref-159" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-159&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-159" id="mwBPQ"><span id="mwBPU"><span id="mwBPY">[</span>158<span id="mwBPc">]</span></span></a></sup> But instead of African Americans as victims, the race riots "represent backlash violence in response to recent Latino and Asian immigration into African American neighborhoods".<sup about="#mwt549" id="cite_ref-Bergesen_&amp;_Herman_160-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Bergesen &amp; Herman&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Bergesen_&amp;_Herman-160&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Bergesen_&amp;_Herman-160" id="mwBPg"><span id="mwBPk"><span id="mwBPo">[</span>159<span id="mwBPs">]</span></span></a></sup>

Social commentator [Mike Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Davis_(scholar) "Mike Davis (scholar)") points to the growing economic disparity in Los Angeles, caused by corporate restructuring and government [deregulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deregulation "Deregulation"), with inner-city residents bearing the brunt of such changes; such conditions engendered a widespread feeling of frustration and powerlessness in the urban populace, who reacted to the King verdicts with a violent expression of collective public protest.<sup about="#mwt552" id="cite_ref-161" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-161&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-161" id="mwBP8"><span id="mwBQA"><span id="mwBQE">[</span>160<span id="mwBQI">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt555" id="cite_ref-162" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-162&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-162" id="mwBQM"><span id="mwBQQ"><span id="mwBQU">[</span>161<span id="mwBQY">]</span></span></a></sup> To Davis and other writers, the tensions between African Americans and Korean Americans had as much to do with the economic competition between the two groups caused by wider market forces as with cultural misunderstandings and anger about the killing of Latasha Harlins.<sup about="#mwt556" id="cite_ref-Kwong_60-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Kwong&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Kwong-60" id="mwBQc"><span id="mwBQg"><span id="mwBQk">[</span>59<span id="mwBQo">]</span></span></a></sup>

Davis wrote that the 1992 Los Angeles Riots were still remembered over 20 years later and that not many changes had yet occurred; conditions of economic inequality, lack of jobs available for Black and Latino youth, and civil liberty violations by law enforcement had remained largely unaddressed years later. Davis described this as a "conspiracy of silence", especially in view of statements made by the Los Angeles Police Department that they would make reforms coming to little fruition. Davis argued that the rioting was different from in the 1965 [Watts Riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watts_Riots "Watts Riots"), which had been more unified among all minorities living in [Watts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watts,_Los_Angeles "Watts, Los Angeles") and South Central; the 1992 riots, on the other hand, were characterized by divided uproars that defied description of a simple uprising of Black against white and involved the destruction and looting of many businesses owned by racial minorities.<sup about="#mwt559" id="cite_ref-163" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-163&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-163" id="mwBQ4"><span id="mwBQ8"><span id="mwBRA">[</span>162<span id="mwBRE">]</span></span></a></sup>

A Special Committee of the California Legislature also studied the riots, producing a report entitled _To Rebuild is Not Enough_.<sup about="#mwt560" id="cite_ref-164" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-164&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-164" id="mwBRQ"><span id="mwBRU"><span id="mwBRY">[</span>163<span id="mwBRc">]</span></span></a></sup> The Committee concluded that the inner-city conditions of poverty, racial segregation, lack of educational and employment opportunities, [police abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Police_brutality "Police brutality") and unequal consumer services created the underlying causes of the riots. It also noted that the decline of industrial jobs in the American economy and the growing ethnic diversity of Los Angeles had contributed to urban problems. Another official report, _The City in Crisis_, was initiated by the Los Angeles Board of Police Commissioners; it made many of the same observations as the Assembly Special Committee about the growth of popular urban dissatisfaction.<sup about="#mwt561" id="cite_ref-165" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-165&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-165" id="mwBRo"><span id="mwBRs"><span id="mwBRw">[</span>164<span id="mwBR0">]</span></span></a></sup> In their study, Farrell and Johnson found similar factors, including the diversification of the L.A. population, the tension between the successful Korean businesses and other minorities, and excessive force on minorities by LAPD and the effect of laissez-faire business on urban employment opportunities.<sup about="#mwt562" id="cite_ref-166" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-166&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-166" id="mwBR4"><span id="mwBR8"><span id="mwBSA">[</span>165<span id="mwBSE">]</span></span></a></sup>
