Rioters were believed to have been motivated by racial tensions but these are considered one of numerous factors.<sup about="#mwt563" id="cite_ref-167" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-167&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-167" id="mwBSM"><span id="mwBSQ"><span id="mwBSU">[</span>166<span id="mwBSY">]</span></span></a></sup> Urban sociologist Joel Kotkin said, "This wasn't a race riot, it was a class riot."<sup about="#mwt564" id="cite_ref-mathewsetal_168-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;mathewsetal&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-mathewsetal-168&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-mathewsetal-168" id="mwBSc"><span id="mwBSg"><span id="mwBSk">[</span>167<span id="mwBSo">]</span></span></a></sup> Many ethnic groups participated in rioting, not only African Americans. _Newsweek_ reported that "Hispanics and even some whites; men, women, and children mingled with African Americans."<sup about="#mwt565" id="cite_ref-mathewsetal_168-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;mathewsetal&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-mathewsetal-168" id="mwBSw"><span id="mwBS0"><span id="mwBS4">[</span>167<span id="mwBS8">]</span></span></a></sup> When residents who lived near Florence and Normandie were asked why they believed riots had occurred in their neighborhoods, they responded to the perceived racist attitudes they had felt throughout their lifetime and empathized with the bitterness the rioters felt.<sup about="#mwt566" id="cite_ref-Dunn_169-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Dunn&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Dunn-169&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Dunn-169" id="mwBTA"><span id="mwBTE"><span id="mwBTI">[</span>168<span id="mwBTM">]</span></span></a></sup> Residents who had respectable jobs, homes, and material items still felt like second class citizens.<sup about="#mwt567" id="cite_ref-Dunn_169-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Dunn&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Dunn-169" id="mwBTQ"><span id="mwBTU"><span id="mwBTY">[</span>168<span id="mwBTc">]</span></span></a></sup> A poll by _Newsweek_ asked whether Black people charged with crimes were treated more harshly or more leniently than other ethnicities; 75% of Black people responded "more harshly", versus 46% of white people.<sup about="#mwt568" id="cite_ref-mathewsetal_168-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;mathewsetal&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-mathewsetal-168" id="mwBTk"><span id="mwBTo"><span id="mwBTs">[</span>167<span id="mwBTw">]</span></span></a></sup>

In his public statements during the riots, [Jesse Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Jackson "Jesse Jackson"), civil rights leader, sympathized with African Americans' anger about the verdicts in the King trial and noted the root causes of the disturbances. He repeatedly emphasized the continuing patterns of racism, police brutality, and economic despair suffered by inner-city residents.<sup about="#mwt569" id="cite_ref-170" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-170&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-170" id="mwBT8"><span id="mwBUA"><span id="mwBUE">[</span>169<span id="mwBUI">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt570" id="cite_ref-171" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-171&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-171" id="mwBUM"><span id="mwBUQ"><span id="mwBUU">[</span>170<span id="mwBUY">]</span></span></a></sup>

Several prominent writers discussed a similar "[culture of poverty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_poverty "Culture of poverty")" argument. Writers in _Newsweek_, for example, drew a distinction between the actions of the rioters in 1992 with those of the urban upheavals in the 1960s, arguing that "\[w\]here the looting at [Watts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watts_riots "Watts riots") had been desperate, angry, mean, the mood this time was closer to a manic fiesta, a TV game show with every looter a winner."<sup about="#mwt571" id="cite_ref-mathewsetal_168-3" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;mathewsetal&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-mathewsetal-168" id="mwBUs"><span id="mwBUw"><span id="mwBU0">[</span>167<span id="mwBU4">]</span></span></a></sup>

According to a 2019 study in the _American Political Science Review_ found that the riots caused a liberal shift, both in the short-term and long-term, politically.<sup about="#mwt574" id="cite_ref-172" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-172&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-172" id="mwBVE"><span id="mwBVI"><span id="mwBVM">[</span>171<span id="mwBVQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

The 1992 events in Los Angeles were compared to the May 2020 police [murder of George Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd") in the US city of [Minneapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneapolis "Minneapolis") that resulted in a global [protest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Floyd_protests "George Floyd protests") movement against police brutality and structural racism.<sup about="#mwt577" id="cite_ref-173" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-173&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-173" id="mwBVk"><span id="mwBVo"><span id="mwBVs">[</span>172<span id="mwBVw">]</span></span></a></sup> Floyd's murder served as an inflection point after the police killing of Breonna Taylor in Louisville, Kentucky in March 2020, fueling public outrage. Unlike in 1992, participants who protested Floyd's murder were more racially diverse and there was little if any racially motivated violence.<sup about="#mwt580" id="cite_ref-174" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-174&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-174" id="mwBV0"><span id="mwBV4"><span id="mwBV8">[</span>173<span id="mwBWA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt583" id="cite_ref-175" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-175&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-175" id="mwBWE"><span id="mwBWI"><span id="mwBWM">[</span>174<span id="mwBWQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

In a 2025 _New York Times_ article, author Joe Domanick contrasted the 1992 Los Angeles riots with the [anti-immigration protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_2025_Los_Angeles_protests "June 2025 Los Angeles protests"), noting the former's widespread violence and systemic collapse after the Rodney King verdict. The 2025 demonstrations and protests, largely Latino-led, have been more focused and less destructive. Domanick highlighted the unique position of Latino officers—many with immigrant roots—caught between community and federal authority, reflecting the evolving racial and political landscape since the 1992 uprising.<sup about="#mwt586" id="cite_ref-NYT2025_176-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYT2025&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NYT2025-176&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYT2025-176" id="mwBWg"><span id="mwBWk"><span id="mwBWo">[</span>175<span id="mwBWs">]</span></span></a></sup>

Democratic presidential candidate [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") said that the violence resulted from the breakdown of economic opportunities and social institutions in the inner city. He also berated both major political parties for failing to address urban issues, especially the Republican Administration for its presiding over "more than a decade of urban decay" generated by their spending cuts.<sup about="#mwt590" id="cite_ref-Brownstein_177-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Brownstein&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Brownstein-177&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Brownstein-177" id="mwBW8"><span id="mwBXA"><span id="mwBXE">[</span>176<span id="mwBXI">]</span></span></a></sup> He also maintained that the King verdicts could not be avenged by the "savage behavior" of "lawless vandals" and stated that people "are looting because ... \[t\]hey do not share our values, and their children are growing up in a culture alien from ours, without family, without neighborhood, without church, without support."<sup about="#mwt591" id="cite_ref-Brownstein_177-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Brownstein&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Brownstein-177" id="mwBXM"><span id="mwBXQ"><span id="mwBXU">[</span>176<span id="mwBXY">]</span></span></a></sup> While Los Angeles was mostly unaffected by the [urban decay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_decay "Urban decay") the other metropolitan areas of the nation faced since the 1960s, racial tensions had been present since the late 1970s, becoming increasingly violent as the 1980s progressed.<sup about="#mwt587" id="mwBXk"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2016)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

Democrat [Maxine Waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxine_Waters "Maxine Waters"), the African American Congressional representative of South Central Los Angeles, said that the events in Los Angeles constituted a "rebellion" or "insurrection," caused by the underlying reality of poverty and despair existing in the inner city. This state of affairs, she asserted, was brought about by a government that had all but abandoned the poor and failed to help compensate for the loss of local jobs and the institutional discrimination encountered by racial minorities, especially at the police's hands and financial institutions.<sup about="#mwt594" id="cite_ref-178" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-178&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-178" id="mwBXw"><span id="mwBX0"><span id="mwBX4">[</span>177<span id="mwBX8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt597" id="cite_ref-Waters_179-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Waters&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Waters-179&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Waters-179" id="mwBYA"><span id="mwBYE"><span id="mwBYI">[</span>178<span id="mwBYM">]</span></span></a></sup>

Conversely, President Bush argued that the unrest was "purely criminal". Though he acknowledged that the King verdicts were plainly unjust, he said that "we simply cannot condone violence as a way of changing the system ... Mob brutality, the total loss of respect for human life was sickeningly sad ... What we saw last night and the night before in Los Angeles is not about civil rights. It's not about the great cause of equality that all Americans must uphold. It's not a message of protest. It's been the brutality of a mob, pure and simple."<sup about="#mwt600" id="cite_ref-180" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-180&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-180" id="mwBYU"><span id="mwBYY"><span id="mwBYc">[</span>179<span id="mwBYg">]</span></span></a></sup>

Vice President [Dan Quayle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Quayle "Dan Quayle") blamed the violence on a "Poverty of Values" – "I believe the lawless social anarchy which we saw is directly related to the breakdown of family structure, personal responsibility and social order in too many areas of our society."<sup about="#mwt603" id="cite_ref-181" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-181&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-181" id="mwBYs"><span id="mwBYw"><span id="mwBY0">[</span>180<span id="mwBY4">]</span></span></a></sup> Similarly, [White House Press Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Press_Secretary "White House Press Secretary") [Marlin Fitzwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlin_Fitzwater "Marlin Fitzwater") alleged that "many of the root problems that have resulted in inner-city difficulties were started in the 1960s and 1970s and ... they have failed ... \[N\]ow we are paying the price."<sup about="#mwt604" id="cite_ref-182" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-182&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-182" id="mwBZE"><span id="mwBZI"><span id="mwBZM">[</span>181<span id="mwBZQ">]</span></span></a></sup>

Writers for former Congressman [Ron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul "Ron Paul") framed the riots in similar terms in the June 1992 edition of the _Ron Paul Political Newsletter_, billed as a special issue focusing on "racial terrorism".<sup about="#mwt607" id="cite_ref-183" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-183&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-183" id="mwBZg"><span id="mwBZk"><span id="mwBZo">[</span>182<span id="mwBZs">]</span></span></a></sup> "Order was only restored in LA", the newsletter read, "when it came time for the blacks to pick up their welfare checks three days after rioting began ... What if the checks had never arrived? No doubt, the blacks would have fully privatized the welfare state through continued looting. But they were paid off, and the violence subsided."<sup about="#mwt610" id="cite_ref-184" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-184&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-184" id="mwBZw"><span id="mwBZ0"><span id="mwBZ4">[</span>183<span id="mwBZ8">]</span></span></a></sup> Paul later disavowed the newsletter and stated he did not exercise direct oversight on its content, but accepted "moral responsibility" for it being published under his name.<sup about="#mwt613" id="cite_ref-185" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-185&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-185" id="mwBaA"><span id="mwBaE"><span id="mwBaI">[</span>184<span id="mwBaM">]</span></span></a></sup>

In the aftermath of the riots, public pressure mounted for a retrial of the officers. Federal charges of [civil rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights "Civil rights") violations were brought against them. As the first anniversary of the acquittal neared, the city tensely awaited the federal jury's decision.

The decision was read in a court session on Saturday, April 17, 1993, at 7 a.m. Officer Laurence Powell and Sergeant [Stacey Koon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stacey_Koon "Stacey Koon") were found guilty, while officers Theodore Briseno and Timothy Wind were acquitted. Mindful of criticism of sensationalist reporting after the first trial and during the riots, media outlets opted for more sober coverage.<sup about="#mwt618" id="cite_ref-186" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-186&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-186" id="mwBas"><span id="mwBaw"><span id="mwBa0">[</span>185<span id="mwBa4">]</span></span></a></sup> Police were fully mobilized with officers on 12 hour shifts, convoy patrols, scout helicopters, street barricades, tactical command centers, and support from the [Army National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_National_Guard "Army National Guard"), the active duty Army and the Marines.<sup about="#mwt621" id="cite_ref-187" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-187&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-187" id="mwBbA"><span id="mwBbE"><span id="mwBbI">[</span>186<span id="mwBbM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt624" id="cite_ref-188" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-188&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-188" id="mwBbQ"><span id="mwBbU"><span id="mwBbY">[</span>187<span id="mwBbc">]</span></span></a></sup>

All four of the officers left or were fired from the LAPD. Briseno left the LAPD after being acquitted on both state and federal charges. Wind, who was also twice acquitted, was fired after the appointment of [Willie L. Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_L._Williams "Willie L. Williams") as Chief of Police. The Los Angeles Police Commission declined to renew Williams's contract, citing failure to fulfill his mandate to create meaningful change in the department.<sup about="#mwt627" id="cite_ref-189" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-189&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-189" id="mwBbo"><span id="mwBbs"><span id="mwBbw">[</span>188<span id="mwBb0">]</span></span></a></sup>

Susan Clemmer, an officer who gave crucial testimony for the defense during the officers' first trial, committed [suicide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide "Suicide") in July 2009 in the lobby of a Los Angeles Sheriff's Station. She had ridden in the ambulance with King and testified that he was laughing and spat blood on her uniform. She had remained in law enforcement and was a Sheriff's Detective at the time of her death.<sup about="#mwt630" id="cite_ref-clemmer-ap_190-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;clemmer-ap&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-clemmer-ap-190&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-clemmer-ap-190" id="mwBcA"><span id="mwBcE"><span id="mwBcI">[</span>189<span id="mwBcM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt633" id="cite_ref-191" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-191&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-191" id="mwBcQ"><span id="mwBcU"><span id="mwBcY">[</span>190<span id="mwBcc">]</span></span></a></sup>

Rodney King was awarded $3.8 million in damages from the City of Los Angeles. He invested most of this money in founding a hip-hop record label, "Straight Alta-Pazz Records". The venture was unable to garner success and soon folded. King was later arrested at least eleven times on a variety of charges, including domestic abuse and hit and run.<sup about="#mwt634" id="cite_ref-TIME_57-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;TIME&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-TIME-57" id="mwBck"><span id="mwBco"><span id="mwBcs">[</span>56<span id="mwBcw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt637" id="cite_ref-NYT_20040919_192-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;NYT_20040919&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-NYT_20040919-192&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-NYT_20040919-192" id="mwBc0"><span id="mwBc4"><span id="mwBc8">[</span>191<span id="mwBdA">]</span></span></a></sup> King and his family moved from Los Angeles to [San Bernardino County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Bernardino_County,_California "San Bernardino County, California")'s [Rialto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rialto,_California "Rialto, California") suburb in an attempt to escape the fame and notoriety and begin a new life.

King and his family later returned to Los Angeles, where they ran a family-owned construction company. Until his death on June 17, 2012, King rarely discussed the night of his beating by police or its aftermath, preferring to remain out of the spotlight. King died of an accidental drowning; authorities said that he had alcohol and drugs in his body. Renee Campbell, his most recent attorney, described King as "... simply a very nice man caught in a very unfortunate situation."<sup about="#mwt640" id="cite_ref-SpotTV_193-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;SpotTV&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-SpotTV-193&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-SpotTV-193" id="mwBdQ"><span id="mwBdU"><span id="mwBdY">[</span>192<span id="mwBdc">]</span></span></a></sup>

On May 3, 1992, in view of the large number of persons arrested during the riots, the [California Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Supreme_Court "California Supreme Court") extended the deadline to charge defendants from 48 hours to 96 hours. That day, 6,345 people were arrested.<sup about="#mwt643" id="cite_ref-Reinhold_20-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Reinhold&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Reinhold-20&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Reinhold-20" id="mwBds"><span id="mwBdw"><span id="mwBd0">[</span>19<span id="mwBd4">]</span></span></a></sup> Nearly one third of the rioters arrested were released because police officers were unable to identify individuals in the sheer volume of the crowd. In one case, officers arrested around 40 people stealing from one store; while they were identifying them, a group of another 12 looters were brought in. With the groups mingled, charges could not be brought against individuals for stealing from specific stores, and the police had to release them all.<sup about="#mwt646" id="cite_ref-194" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-194&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-194" id="mwBd8"><span id="mwBeA"><span id="mwBeE">[</span>193<span id="mwBeI">]</span></span></a></sup>

In the weeks after the rioting, more than 11,000 people were arrested.<sup about="#mwt650" id="cite_ref-Oh_195-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Oh&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Oh-195&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Oh-195" id="mwBeQ"><span id="mwBeU"><span id="mwBeY">[</span>194<span id="mwBec">]</span></span></a></sup> Many of the looters in Black communities were turned in by their neighbors, who were angry about the destruction of businesses who employed locals and provided basic needs such as groceries. Many of the looters, fearful of prosecution by law enforcement and condemnation from their neighbors, ended up placing looted items curbside in other neighborhoods to get rid of them.<sup about="#mwt647" id="mwBek"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (November 2021)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup>

[![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Los_Angeles_Riots,_1992_(17094267471).jpg)

Remains of a burned building

After three days of arson and looting, some 3,767 buildings were affected and damaged<sup about="#mwt651" id="cite_ref-Rein_196-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Rein&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Rein-196&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Rein-196" id="mwBfA"><span id="mwBfE"><span id="mwBfI">[</span>195<span id="mwBfM">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt654" id="cite_ref-197" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-197&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-197" id="mwBfQ"><span id="mwBfU"><span id="mwBfY">[</span>196<span id="mwBfc">]</span></span></a></sup> and property damage was estimated at more than $1 billion.<sup about="#mwt655" id="cite_ref-cnn_fast_fact_53-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;cnn fast fact&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-cnn_fast_fact-53" id="mwBfg"><span id="mwBfk"><span id="mwBfo">[</span>52<span id="mwBfs">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt658" id="cite_ref-Tomaszewski_198-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Tomaszewski&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Tomaszewski-198&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Tomaszewski-198" id="mwBfw"><span id="mwBf0"><span id="mwBf4">[</span>197<span id="mwBf8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt661" id="cite_ref-Alonso,_Alex_A._199-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Alonso, Alex A.&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Alonso,_Alex_A.-199&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Alonso,_Alex_A.-199" id="mwBgA"><span id="mwBgE"><span id="mwBgI">[</span>198<span id="mwBgM">]</span></span></a></sup> Donations were given to help with food and medicine. The office of State Senator [Diane E. Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_E._Watson "Diane E. Watson") provided shovels and brooms to volunteers from all over the community who helped clean. Thirteen thousand police and military personnel were on patrol, protecting intact gas stations and food stores; they reopened along with other businesses areas such as the [Universal Studios tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_tour "Universal Studios tour"), dance halls, and bars. Many organizations stepped forward to rebuild Los Angeles; South Central's [Operation Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_HOPE,_Inc. "Operation HOPE, Inc.") and [Koreatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koreatown,_Los_Angeles "Koreatown, Los Angeles")'s Saigu and KCCD (Korean Churches for Community Development), all raised millions to repair destruction and improve economic development.<sup about="#mwt664" id="cite_ref-Ramirez_200-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Ramirez&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Ramirez-200&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Ramirez-200" id="mwBgg"><span id="mwBgk"><span id="mwBgo">[</span>199<span id="mwBgs">]</span></span></a></sup> Singer [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson") "donated $1.25 million to start a health counseling service for inner-city kids".<sup about="#mwt665" id="cite_ref-201" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-201&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-201" id="mwBg0"><span id="mwBg4"><span id="mwBg8">[</span>200<span id="mwBhA">]</span></span></a></sup> President [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") signed a declaration of disaster; it activated federal relief efforts for the victims of looting and arson, which included grants and low-cost loans to cover their property losses.<sup about="#mwt666" id="cite_ref-Rein_196-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Rein&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Rein-196" id="mwBhI"><span id="mwBhM"><span id="mwBhQ">[</span>195<span id="mwBhU">]</span></span></a></sup> The Rebuild LA program promised $6 billion in private investment to create 74,000 jobs.<sup about="#mwt667" id="cite_ref-Alonso,_Alex_A._199-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Alonso, Alex A.&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Alonso,_Alex_A.-199" id="mwBhc"><span id="mwBhg"><span id="mwBhk">[</span>198<span id="mwBho">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt670" id="cite_ref-Hayden_202-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Hayden&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Hayden-202&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Hayden-202" id="mwBhs"><span id="mwBhw"><span id="mwBh0">[</span>201<span id="mwBh4">]</span></span></a></sup>

The majority of the local stores were never rebuilt.<sup about="#mwt673" id="cite_ref-McDonald_203-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;McDonald&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-McDonald-203&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-McDonald-203" id="mwBiA"><span id="mwBiE"><span id="mwBiI">[</span>202<span id="mwBiM">]</span></span></a></sup> Store owners had difficulty getting loans; myths about the city or at least certain neighborhoods of it arose discouraging investment and preventing growth of employment.<sup about="#mwt676" id="cite_ref-Larson_204-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Larson&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Larson-204&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Larson-204" id="mwBiQ"><span id="mwBiU"><span id="mwBiY">[</span>203<span id="mwBic">]</span></span></a></sup> Few of the rebuilding plans were implemented, and business investors and some community members rejected South L.A.<sup about="#mwt677" id="cite_ref-Alonso,_Alex_A._199-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Alonso, Alex A.&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Alonso,_Alex_A.-199" id="mwBig"><span id="mwBik"><span id="mwBio">[</span>198<span id="mwBis">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt678" id="cite_ref-McDonald_203-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;McDonald&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-McDonald-203" id="mwBiw"><span id="mwBi0"><span id="mwBi4">[</span>202<span id="mwBi8">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt681" id="cite_ref-205" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-205&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-205" id="mwBjA"><span id="mwBjE"><span id="mwBjI">[</span>204<span id="mwBjM">]</span></span></a></sup>

Many Los Angeles residents bought weapons for self-defense against further violence. The 10-day waiting period in California law stymied those who wanted to purchase firearms while the riot was going on.<sup about="#mwt684" id="cite_ref-206" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-206&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-206" id="mwBjY"><span id="mwBjc"><span id="mwBjg">[</span>205<span id="mwBjk">]</span></span></a></sup>

In a survey of local residents in 2010, 77 percent felt that the economic situation in Los Angeles had significantly worsened since 1992.<sup about="#mwt685" id="cite_ref-Ramirez_200-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Ramirez&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Ramirez-200" id="mwBjs"><span id="mwBjw"><span id="mwBj0">[</span>199<span id="mwBj4">]</span></span></a></sup> From 1992 to 2007, the Black population dropped by 123,000, while the Latino population grew more than 450,000.<sup about="#mwt686" id="cite_ref-McDonald_203-2" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;McDonald&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-McDonald-203" id="mwBj8"><span id="mwBkA"><span id="mwBkE">[</span>202<span id="mwBkI">]</span></span></a></sup> According to the Los Angeles police statistics, violent crime fell by 76 percent between 1992 and 2010, which was a period of declining crime across the country. It was accompanied by lessening tensions between racial groups.<sup about="#mwt689" id="cite_ref-HeraldNet_207-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;HeraldNet&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-HeraldNet-207&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-HeraldNet-207" id="mwBkM"><span id="mwBkQ"><span id="mwBkU">[</span>206<span id="mwBkY">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2012, sixty percent of residents reported racial tension had improved in the past 20 years, and the majority said gang activity had also decreased.<sup about="#mwt690" id="cite_ref-208" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-208&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-208" id="mwBkc"><span id="mwBkg"><span id="mwBkk">[</span>207<span id="mwBko">]</span></span></a></sup>

Multiple filmmakers, musical artists and other creatives have produced works that were influenced by, reference, or are a direct response to the 1992 riots. Several scripted television shows worked the riots into episodes as a plot point, both immediately after the events and years later. The NBC sitcom _[A Different World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Different_World "A Different World")_ featured two of their characters travelling to Los Angeles just as the riots started, while the [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") comedy series _[In Living Color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_Living_Color "In Living Color")_ had the riots as a reoccurring topic during their third season. Other shows that incorporated the riots into their stories included _[Beverly Hills, 90210](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_90210 "Beverly Hills, 90210")_, _[Doogie Howser, M.D.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doogie_Howser,_M.D. "Doogie Howser, M.D.")_, and _[The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fresh_Prince_of_Bel-Air "The Fresh Prince of Multiple musical artists and bands have referenced or responded to the riots via their works. [Sublime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sublime_(band) "Sublime (band)")'s self-titled album "[Sublime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sublime_(album) "Sublime (album)")", track five "[April 29, 1992 (Miami)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/April_29,_1992_(Miami) "April 29, 1992 (Miami)")", features lead singer [Bradley Nowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Nowell "Bradley Nowell") portraying himself as one of the rioters, describing the events and calling out the meaning of the riots running much deeper than [Rodney King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_King "Rodney King")'s assault. [Ice Cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ice_Cube "Ice Cube") has written several songs that reference the riots such as "We Had to Tear This Motherfucka Up",<sup about="#mwt758" id="cite_ref-230" Other areas where the riots have been influential include literature,<sup about="#mwt773" id="cite_ref-235" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-235&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-235" id="mwBu8"><span id="mwBvA"><span id="mwBvE">[</span>234<span id="mwBvI">]</span></span></a></sup> theater,<sup about="#mwt776" id="cite_ref-236" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-236&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-236" id="mwBvM"><span id="mwBvQ"><span id="mwBvU">[</span>235<span id="mwBvY">]</span></span></a></sup> and video games. The titular city of the 2004 video game _[Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Theft_Auto:_San_Andreas "Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas")_ was modeled after Los Angeles and the acquittal of a corrupt police officer causes riots throughout the city that use the 1992 riots as a reference.<sup about="#mwt779" id="cite_ref-237" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-237&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-237" id="mwBvk"><span id="mwBvo"><span id="mwBvs">[</span>236<span id="mwBvw">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt782" id="cite_ref-Wills_238-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Wills&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Wills-238&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Wills-238" id="mwBv0"><span id="mwBv4"><span id="mwBv8">[</span>237<span id="mwBwA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt785" id="cite_ref-Jahn-Sudmann_239-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;ref&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;name&quot;:&quot;Jahn-Sudmann&quot;},&quot;body&quot;:{&quot;id&quot;:&quot;mw-reference-text-cite_note-Jahn-Sudmann-239&quot;}}"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Los_Angeles_riots#cite_note-Jahn-Sudmann-239" id="mwBwE"><span id="mwBwI"><span id="mwBwM">[</span>238<span id="mwBwQ">]</span></span></a></sup>
